title: Impact of prolonged balloon inflation on valve expansion and early clinical outcomes following contemporary balloon-expandable transcatheter aortic valve implantation.
authors: Francesco Cardaioli; Luca Nai Fovino; Tommaso Fabris; Giulia Masiero; Andrea Panza; Massimo Napodano; Chiara Fraccaro; Francesco Putortì; Giuseppe Tarantini
journal: EuroIntervention : journal of EuroPCR in collaboration with the Working Group on Interventional Cardiology of the European Society of Cardiology
abstract:
Incomplete expansion of balloon-expandable (BE) transcatheter heart valves (THVs) after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) may affect valve performance and durability. Routine THV post-dilatation (the "double-tap" technique) has been proposed to optimise device expansion; however, it may increase procedural complexity.
We sought to evaluate the impact of a prolonged balloon inflation implantation strategy on BE THV expansion, haemodynamic performance, and early clinical outcomes.
This single-centre study analysed consecutive TAVI patients treated for native tricuspid aortic stenosis with the SAPIEN 3 Ultra RESILIA THV using a prolonged balloon inflation strategy (8 seconds). Valve expansion was assessed by fluoroscopy at multiple frame levels and compared with three validated reference standards. Results were also descriptively compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique. Clinical and haemodynamic outcomes at 30 days were adjudicated according to Valve Academic Research Consortium 3 criteria.
A total of 84 patients (mean age 78.8 years, 58% male, median Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score 3.9%) were included. Prolonged inflation resulted in complete THV expansion at the inflow and outflow levels, with only mild underexpansion (98.5±1.3%) detected at the midframe level when manufacturer-defined nominal values were used as the reference. When compared with previously published data on the double-tap technique, expansion values for the 23, 26, and 29 mm valves were consistently similar or higher, whereas lower expansion was observed for the 20 mm size. Device success was achieved in all cases, with no stroke at 30 days. Permanent pacemaker implantation occurred in 6% of patients. Haemodynamic performance was favourable (mean gradient 9.2 [interquartile range 7.0-10.3] mmHg at 30 days), with no patients having moderate or severe paravalvular leak.
Prolonged balloon inflation during BE THV deployment is associated with favourable valve expansion, haemodynamic results, and a favourable safety profile, consistent with values reported in double-tap series. If confirmed in larger studies, this strategy may represent a simple alternative to routine double-tap in selected patients.

title: Tracking Active Fibroblast-Mediated Tissue Remodelling in Cardiomyopathies: Translational Insights from FAPI PET Imaging.
authors: Inês Fortuna; Janete Santos; Paula Soeiro; Raquel Machado; Ana Oliveira; Jorge Pereira; Giuseppe Limongelli; Teresa Faria; Elisabete Martins; European Reference Network for Rare, Low-Prevalence, or Complex Diseases of the Heart (ERN GUARD-Heart)
abstract: Myocardial fibrosis is a major pathological component of cardiac remodelling and contributes to ventricular stiffness, impaired myocardial function, heart failure progression, and arrhythmic vulnerability across a broad spectrum of cardiomyopathies. In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM), fibrotic remodelling encompasses both diffuse interstitial matrix expansion and focal replacement fibrosis and is closely associated with disease severity and adverse clinical outcomes. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR), using late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) and quantitative parametric mapping, is central to non-invasive myocardial tissue characterization. LGE primarily identifies focal areas of replacement fibrosis and scar, whereas native T1, T2, and extracellular volume (ECV) mapping provide complementary information on diffuse myocardial and interstitial tissue abnormalities, including extracellular matrix expansion. However, these techniques characterize the structural and tissue-level consequences of myocardial injury and remodelling rather than directly visualizing the cellular processes underlying fibroblast activation. Fibroblast activation protein inhibitor positron emission tomography (FAPI PET) has emerged as a promising molecular imaging approach for assessing active fibroblast-mediated tissue remodelling. By targeting fibroblast activation protein (FAP), a cell-surface serine protease upregulated in activated fibroblasts and myofibroblasts. FAPI radiotracers may provide a molecular readout of accessible FAP expression that complements structural and tissue characterization by CMR. This review examines the cellular and molecular mechanisms underlying active myocardial remodelling, with particular emphasis on transforming growth factor-β1 (TGF-β1)/Smad signalling, fibroblast-to-myofibroblast transition, FAP expression, and extracellular matrix turnover. We critically evaluate the current clinical evidence for FAPI PET/CT and hybrid PET/CMR across cardiomyopathies, focusing on HCM while also considering ischemic, inflammatory, infiltrative, and other non-ischemic forms of cardiac remodelling. Particular attention is given to the relationship between myocardial FAPI uptake, CMR tissue characterization, ventricular function, circulating biomarkers, and calculated arrhythmic risk. Although initial studies support the complementary value of FAPI PET and CMR for characterizing active and established myocardial remodelling, the available evidence remains limited by small, predominantly single-centre cohorts, heterogeneous radiotracers and acquisition protocols, and the absence of validated quantitative thresholds or prospective outcome data. Larger longitudinal studies are required to determine whether FAPI PET can provide incremental prognostic information or serve as a reproducible imaging biomarker for disease progression and therapeutic response.

title: Structural Optimization and Fatigue Performance Evaluation of Balloon-Expandable Aortic Valve Stents.
authors: Tao Cai; Chaoqun Zhao; Gang Fang
abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is a critical therapy for aortic stenosis, but most existing valve stents are designed for Western patients, whose aortic root anatomy differs from Chinese patients characterized by smaller annulus diameters, heavier calcification, and a higher prevalence of bicuspid valves. To address this mismatch, we designed a balloon-expandable aortic valve stent tailored for Chinese patients and systematically evaluated its performance. Four structural schemes were considered; a diamond-hexagonal composite mesh was selected based on radial strength, expansion uniformity, anchoring stability, sealing, and coronary access. Material properties of MP35N were obtained via tensile tests, and finite element models simulated crimping, recoil, and expansion. Among three end-corner geometries, the U-shaped design showed superior mechanical behavior with lower stress/strain concentrations. For stents crimped to 6.5 mm, maximum equivalent stress ranged from 1030 to 1076 MPa and plastic strain from 0.221 to 0.259; upon expansion to 20-29 mm, stress reached 1417-1493 MPa and strain 0.447-0.544, with strain concentrated at the corner ends. Simulated recoil matched experimental results within 7% relative error. Accelerated fatigue testing (4 × 108 cycles) of the bare stents revealed no fractures, displacements, or surface damage. These findings demonstrate that the optimized bare stent structure exhibits good mechanical feasibility, durability, and improved anatomical compatibility for Chinese TAVI patients, providing a promising device solution for domestic clinical application.

title: Kidney Function Trajectories in Patients with and Without Chronic Kidney Disease Undergoing Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Single-Retrospective Cohort Study.
authors: Hirofumi Sakuma; Satoshi Kawaguchi; Yuya Kitani; Tatsuya Aonuma; Naoko Kawabata; Erika Saito; Akiho Minoshima; Shingo Kunioka; Hiroyuki Kamiya; Naoki Nakagawa
abstract: Background/Objectives: Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) may improve systemic hemodynamics and kidney perfusion; however, its effect on long-term kidney function remains unclear. We evaluated kidney function trajectories before and after TAVR in patients with and without chronic kidney disease (CKD). Methods: This single-center retrospective cohort study included patients with severe aortic stenosis (AS) who underwent TAVR between June 2016 and December 2024. Overall, 314 eligible patients were classified by baseline estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) as without CKD (≥60 mL/min/1.73 m2) or with CKD (<60 mL/min/1.73 m2). Linear mixed-effects models estimated pre- and post-TAVR eGFR slopes, which were compared between groups after covariate adjustment. Results: Median follow-up was 2.0 years. Adjusted pre-TAVR eGFR slopes were -2.11 (95% confidence interval [CI], -3.34 to -0.89) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients without CKD and -2.83 (95% CI, -3.65 to -2.01) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients with CKD. The post-TAVR slopes were -4.02 (95% CI, -5.68 to -2.35) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients without CKD and -0.83 (95% CI, -2.04 to 0.39) mL/min/1.73 m2/year in patients with CKD, with a significant group difference of 3.19 (95% CI, 1.44 to 4.94) mL/min/1.73 m2/year (p < 0.001). In patients with CKD, the post-TAVR slope improved relative to the pre-TAVR slope by 2.01 (95% CI, 0.51 to 3.50) mL/min/1.73 m2/year (p < 0.01), whereas no significant change was observed in those without CKD. Conclusions: eGFR decline after TAVR was attenuated in patients with CKD compared with those without CKD, suggesting that kidney function may be preserved through hemodynamic improvement following TAVR.

title: Clinical Outcomes of Combined TAVR-PCI Versus SAVR-CABG in Patients with Aortic Stenosis and Coronary Artery Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Ricardo Antonio Rodriguez Mejia; Mathhar Aldaoud; Ifeanyi Momodu; Merina Dongol; Girum Feyissa; Kelechi Aruogu; Zamaraq M Bhatti; Abdul Haseeb Riaz; Nafisa Saleem
abstract: Background/Objectives: Coronary artery disease coexists with severe aortic stenosis in about half of patients. Surgical aortic valve replacement with coronary artery bypass grafting (SAVR+CABG) is guideline-recommended, but transcatheter aortic valve replacement with percutaneous coronary intervention (TAVR+PCI) is increasingly used. Prior meta-analyses double-counted overlapping populations and did not report randomized evidence separately; we re-examined the comparison after correcting both. Methods: PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), Web of Science and ClinicalTrials.gov were searched up to July 2026 for randomized and comparative observational studies, excluding reports with overlapping populations. Outcomes were pooled with random-effects models, stratified by study design, and re-analysed without administrative databases. Certainty was rated with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Results: Fourteen studies were included (two randomized trials, nine cohorts, three administrative databases), comprising 154,892 patients (28,569 TAVR+PCI; 126,323 SAVR+CABG). TAVR+PCI was associated with lower early mortality (odds ratio (OR) 0.60, 95% confidence interval (CI) 0.44-0.84) and less acute kidney injury (OR 0.34, 0.20-0.57), but greater pacemaker implantation (OR 2.18, 1.93-2.46) and major vascular complications (OR 3.38, 1.65-6.89). Stroke, myocardial infarction and one-year mortality (OR 0.80, 0.58-1.10) did not differ; bleeding results were inconsistent (I2 = 95%). Over 12-72 months, mortality was higher with TAVR+PCI (hazard ratio (HR) 1.38, 1.28-1.49; nine observational studies), unchanged without the largest cohort. Administrative databases drove heterogeneity but not the direction of any early outcome. Certainty was moderate for pacemaker implantation and low or very low otherwise; randomized data were too limited to confirm these findings. Conclusions: In predominantly observational evidence, TAVR+PCI was associated with lower early risk but higher mortality over longer follow-up. This trade-off supports individualized Heart Team decisions rather than the superiority of either strategy. Adequately powered randomized trials with long-term follow-up are needed.

title: Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation in Complex Anatomy: An Anatomy-Driven Framework for Bicuspid Stenosis, Pure Aortic Regurgitation, and the Small Annulus in the Era of Lifetime Management.
authors: Daniel Miron Brie; Cristian Mornoș; Roxana Popescu; Alina Diduța Brie
abstract: Background: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation is established for severe calcific tricuspid aortic stenosis, but its application in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) stenosis, pure native aortic regurgitation (AR), and small aortic annulus anatomy remains limited by heterogeneous morphology, device-specific constraints, and uncertain long-term outcomes. These settings require decisions that extend beyond immediate procedural success to encompass coronary access, reintervention, valve durability, and associated aortopathy. This review synthesizes current evidence and proposes an anatomy-driven framework integrating imaging, device selection, procedural planning, and lifetime management. Methods: A structured narrative review was conducted in accordance with the Scale for the Assessment of Narrative Review Articles (SANRA) criteria. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from 1 January 2010 to 31 March 2026 for studies addressing TAVI in BAV stenosis, pure native AR, and small aortic annulus anatomy. Randomized trials, meta-analyses, multicenter registries, pivotal device studies, and guideline or consensus documents were prioritized. After screening 2663 records and assessing 330 full-text reports, 101 records were retained for qualitative synthesis. Evidence was appraised by anatomical substrate, imaging phenotype, device strategy, procedural hazards, and implications for lifetime management. Results: In BAV stenosis, contemporary registry and prospective cohort data support high device success and acceptable early and mid-term outcomes in carefully selected patients; however, calcified raphe, bulky asymmetric leaflet or left ventricular outflow tract calcification, annular eccentricity, and concomitant aortopathy identify higher-risk phenotypes that often favor surgery. Randomized evidence in younger low-risk BAV patients remains limited and exploratory, with the NOTION-2 trial showing a numerically higher 3-year composite event rate after TAVI than surgical aortic valve replacement (20.4% vs. 7.8%; hazard ratio 2.9, 95% confidence interval 0.9-9.0) in the small bicuspid subgroup. In pure native AR, lack of annular calcification and frequent root dilatation impair anchoring of conventional transcatheter heart valves, increasing risks of migration, embolization, residual AR, and second-valve implantation. Dedicated leaflet-anchoring devices have improved outcomes: in ALIGN-AR, the JenaValve Trilogy system achieved procedural success above 95% in high-surgical-risk patients, although evidence remains single-arm and nonrandomized. In small annuli, the strongest comparative evidence comes from the SMART trial, in which supra-annular self-expanding valves were non-inferior to balloon-expandable valves for the 12-month clinical composite and reduced moderate/severe prosthesis-patient mismatch at 30 days (11.2% vs. 35.3%). Across all three phenotypes, electrocardiography-gated computed tomography is fundamental for defining anchoring, sizing, calcium distribution, root and coronary anatomy, anticipated coronary re-access, and the feasibility of redo-TAVI. Surgery remains particularly relevant when aortic repair, annular/root enlargement, or a more durable lifetime strategy is required. Conclusions: TAVI is feasible in selected patients with BAV stenosis, pure native AR, and small aortic annuli, but the evidentiary strength and optimal procedural strategy differ substantially across these anatomies. Treatment should be guided by an anatomy-driven, computed-tomography-based Heart Team assessment that integrates immediate procedural feasibility with age, surgical candidacy, aortopathy, prosthesis-patient mismatch risk, coronary access, durability, and future reintervention options. Surgery remains the more established strategy for many younger, operable patients with unfavorable BAV morphology or aortopathy, AR with root dilatation, or very small annuli amenable to enlargement. Dedicated randomized trials, standardized imaging criteria, and long-term durability data are needed to refine lifetime management in complex aortic valve anatomy.

title: The Cusp-Overlap Technique Versus the Standard Three-Cusp Technique for Self-Expanding Transcatheter Aortic Valves-A Single-Center Experience.
authors: Alexandru Ispas; Damien Brunet; Redouane Saady; Yacoub Habib; Catalin Pestrea; Laurent Drogoul
abstract: Background: Conduction disturbances and the subsequent need for permanent pacemaker implantation (PPMI) remain a major limitation of transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) with self-expanding transcatheter heart valves (SE-THVs). The cusp-overlap technique (COT) has been proposed to optimize implantation depth and reduce PPMI rates compared to the standard three-cusp technique (3CT). Methods: This retrospective, single-center study included 113 consecutive patients with symptomatic severe aortic stenosis who underwent TAVR with the Medtronic CoreValve Evolut™ SE-THV(Medtronic, Minneapolis, MN, USA) between September 2020 and March 2023. Patients were treated using either COT (n = 49) or 3CT (n = 62). Baseline characteristics, procedural outcomes, and 30-day clinical events were compared before and after one-to-one propensity score matching. The primary endpoint was the incidence of PPMI at hospital discharge; the secondary endpoint was a composite of death, stroke, life-threatening or disabling bleeding, major vascular complications, and moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation at 30 days. A post hoc power calculation was performed given the low observed event rate. Results: Procedural success was achieved in 98.2% of patients. In the unmatched cohort, PPMI occurred in 6.1% (COT) vs. 9.7% (3CT) (p = 0.48). In the matched cohort (49 pairs), PPMI rates were 6.1% (COT) vs. 12.2% (3CT) (p = 0.48). With only 3 vs. 6 PPMI events in the matched cohort, the study had an estimated post hoc power of approximately 19% (two-sided α = 0.05) to detect the observed difference, so the negative primary result should be regarded as inconclusive rather than as evidence of equivalence between techniques. The secondary composite endpoint occurred less frequently in the COT group both before matching (14.3% vs. 32.3%; p = 0.049) and after matching (14.3% vs. 30.6%, p = 0.049). This composite difference was driven predominantly by the moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation (PVL) component (12.2% vs. 24.2% unmatched; 12.2% vs. 22.4% matched) rather than by death, stroke, or major vascular complications. Evolut device generation differed markedly by arm (COT patients received later-generation devices far more often than 3CT; p < 0.001), and is presented in the Methods/Results Sections as a key temporal confounder. COT was associated with a lower incidence of moderate/severe paravalvular regurgitation, without prolonging procedural time. Conclusions: In this real-world single-center cohort, the cusp-overlap technique was not associated with a statistically significant reduction in PPMI after TAVR with the CoreValve Evolut™ SE-THV. COT was, however, associated with fewer paravalvular leaks and a lower rate of the secondary composite of adverse clinical events at 30 days.

title: Lipoprotein(a): Particle vs mass and prevalent cardiovascular disease in the cardiovascular risk in Young Finns study population.
authors: Olli Raitakari; Matias Knuuti; Anna Linko-Parvinen; Katja Pahkala; Suvi Rovio; Noora Kartiosuo; Sini Stenbacka; Irina Lisinen; Britt-Marie Loo; Terho Lehtimäki; Mika Kähönen; Claudia Lamina; Florian Kronenberg; Markus Juonala; Jorma S A Viikari; Juha Mykkänen
abstract:
Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] can be reported as mass (mg/dL) or particle concentration (nmol/L). Because Lp(a) acts at the particle level, molar concentration may better reflect biologically relevant exposure.
To compare molar- and mass-based Lp(a) in relation to cardiovascular outcomes, risk classification, LPA genetic variation, and apo(a) isoform phenotype in the Young Finns Study.
Molar Lp(a) was measured using a traceable Roche Tina-quant Gen.2 assay and mass using a nontraceable Thermo Fisher assay. Associations with cardiovascular outcomes and aortic valve stenosis were assessed by logistic regression in adults aged ≥40 years (N = 3898). Agreement was assessed using Bland-Altman analysis and guideline-based risk reclassification. Associations with LPA genetic risk score and apo(a) isoform phenotype were assessed using Spearman correlation.
Both metrics showed similar associations across cardiovascular outcomes, with significant associations for coronary artery disease (CAD) and aortic valve stenosis. In fully adjusted CAD models, the odds ratio for the highest vs lowest quintile was 1.55 for molar and 1.67 for mass. Agreement between guideline-based risk categories was 95.6%. Molar assigned 2.9% of individuals to a higher risk category than mass, vs 1.5% in the opposite direction. The molar-to-mass ratio was associated with LPA score and apo(a) isoform size, with greater attenuation after adjustment for molar than mass.
Molar and mass showed comparable associations with cardiovascular outcomes. However, molar reporting aligned more closely with the genetic and structural determinants of Lp(a) and more often assigned individuals to higher guideline-based risk categories, supporting continued standardization toward particle-based reporting.

title: Aspirin for primary prevention in patients with high lipoprotein(a): A promising therapeutic option while awaiting future therapies?
authors: Francesca Vittone; Giuliana Autiero; Sara Angela Malerba; Elisabetta Grolla; Michele Dalla Vestra
abstract: Elevated lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined cardiovascular risk factor, linked to both atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and aortic valve stenosis. Plasma Lp(a) levels between 30-50mg/dL suggest a moderate risk, while levels of 51-180mg/dL indicate high risk, and concentrations exceeding 180mg/dL are linked to a very high cardiovascular risk. Currently, there are no approved therapies specifically indicated to lower Lp(a). Recent evidences indicate a role of aspirin in reducing cardiovascular events in primary prevention in patients with high Lp(a). In this review, we discuss the results of the studies that explored the impact of aspirin in reducing cardiovascular events in primary prevention in patients with increased Lp(a) while waiting for the results from large-scale research initiative exploring the impact of RNA-targeting Lp(a)-lowering therapies in reducing cardiovascular risk. In conclusion, waiting for the ongoing trials on emerging RNA-based therapies, the use of aspirin in a subgroup of patients with high atherosclerotic cardiovascular risk, with very high Lp(a) levels and without important bleeding risk could be an interesting strategy. Emerging RNA-targeted therapies might offer in future increased protection against the occurrence of major atherosclerotic cardiovascular events compared to standard lipid management agents in these patients.

title: Pelacarsen and Lp(a)HORIZON: Interpreting the Disconnect Between Lipoprotein(a) Lowering and Cardiovascular Outcomes.
authors: Pierre Sabouret; Domenico Mario Giamundo; Elad Asher; Salvatore De Rosa; Giuseppe Andò; Felice Gragnano; Roger S Blumenthal; Dan Atar; Mamas A Mamas
abstract: Lipoprotein(a) [Lp(a)] is a genetically determined causal risk factor for atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and calcific aortic valve stenosis. Pelacarsen, a hepatocyte-directed antisense oligonucleotide targeting apolipoprotein(a), was evaluated in Lp(a)HORIZON, the first large phase 3 cardiovascular outcomes trial specifically designed to test whether pharmacological Lp(a) lowering reduces cardiovascular events. Topline results announced in September 2026 indicated that pelacarsen lowered Lp(a) but did not reduce the primary composite cardiovascular endpoint in patients with established cardiovascular disease. Full trial data are awaited, and the mechanisms underlying this neutral result remain uncertain. We discuss potential explanations, including treatment after prolonged cumulative Lp(a) exposure, advanced vascular disease, intensive background prevention, the magnitude and duration of Lp(a) suppression, patient selection, baseline cardiovascular risk, and biological heterogeneity. We also examine implications for emerging therapies, including olpasiran, zerlasiran, lepodisiran, and muvalaplin, and for the design of ongoing cardiovascular outcome trials.

title: Coronary microvascular dysfunction in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve implantation: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Maethas Panyawongkhanti; Peerawat Chintrakulchai; Chonthicha Tanking; Wongsakorn Luangphiphat
abstract:
Coronary microvascular dysfunction (CMD) is a complication of severe aortic stenosis. Its prevalence after transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) and prognostic significance are understudied, as are the post-TAVI trajectories of microvascular indices.
The aims of this study were to determine the pooled prevalence of CMD, the influence of the diagnostic modality, the post-TAVI coronary flow reserve (CFR) and microvascular resistance changes, and the prognostic impact of baseline CMD on major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI.
Five databases were searched from January 2010 to December 2025 for studies involving adults with severe aortic stenosis undergoing TAVI in which CMD was assessed by wire-based thermodilution, angiography-derived indices, Doppler measurements, or stress cardiac magnetic resonance. The risk of bias and certainty of evidence were assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale and GRADE, respectively. Random-effects meta-analyses (DerSimonian-Laird) pooled CMD prevalence (stratified by modality), CFR change (mean difference; before-after design), and prognostic hazard ratios (HRs). Change in microvascular resistance was synthesized narratively. The protocol was prospectively registered (PROSPERO: CRD42025143775) and reported per the PRISMA 2020 guidance.
Eleven primary studies were analyzed, 10 of which (n = 1,212) contributed to the prevalence analyses. An additional study (n = 126) was included in the sensitivity analyses only. CMD prevalence was 46.8% (95% confidence interval [CI] [34.0, 59.9]; I2 = 72%) and 38.4% (95% CI [35.3, 41.7]; I2 = 0%) when assessed using wire-based thermodilution (k = 6, n = 324) and angiographic (k = 4, n = 888) indices, respectively. CFR increased post-TAVI by a pooled mean difference of +0.49 (95% CI [+0.27, + 0.71]; I2 = 72%; k = 5, n = 103 paired observations). Reductions in microvascular resistance were confined to pressure-to-velocity and reserve ratio indices, and absolute minimal microvascular resistance was unchanged (k = 4, n = 85). The HR for MACE was 3.22 (95% CI [0.98, 10.60]; I2 = 78%; k = 2, n = 585). Substantial heterogeneity reflected non-equivalent CMD definitions.
The prevalence of CMD pre-TAVI is influenced by the diagnostic method. CFR tends to improve after TAVI, likely due to reduced resting demand rather than structural repair. The CMD-MACE association should be viewed as hypothesis-generating due to limited studies, varied CMD definitions, and incompatible HR calculations. Prospective multicenter studies with standardized CMD definitions are required.

title: Diagnostic Performance of a Deep Learning Model Using Phonocardiogram and Single-Lead ECG Signals for Detecting Moderate-or-Greater Aortic Stenosis: Multicenter External Validation.
authors: Shumpei Saito; Masanobu Ishii; Shimpei Ogawa; Hiroshi Seki; Koshiro Ikeda; Youhei Kayano; Yuhei Yasui; Ginga Sato; Mitsuru Ohishi; Takuro Kubozono; Naritatsu Saito; Eri Toda Kato; Masahiro Yamada; Shunsuke Natori; Yuki Kunikane; Takafumi Yokomatsu; Masashi Kato; Yasuaki Sagara; Nami Uchiyama; Nobuhiko Atsuchi; Shota Kawahara; Shoji Natsugoe; Noriaki Tabata; Kenichi Tsujita
abstract:
Valvular heart disease, particularly aortic stenosis (AS), often remains asymptomatic until advanced stages, making early detection challenging. Although cardiac auscultation is a traditional screening tool, its diagnostic accuracy is limited. We aimed to externally validate a deep learning-based model (eAS model) using phonocardiogram (PCG) and single-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) signals to detect moderate-or-greater AS.
PCG and ECG recordings were acquired using a PCG device (Cardio-EGG). Transthoracic echocardiography served as the reference standard. The external validation cohort consisted of 951 patients from 3 medical institutions, including 70 with moderate-or-greater AS. The primary outcome was sensitivity for detecting moderate-or-greater AS; secondary outcomes included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), specificity, predictive values, and likelihood ratios (LR).
The external validation cohort (n = 951, median age 73 years, male 65%) exhibited more advanced valvular disease than the training/development cohort. The eAS model achieved an AUROC of 0.9632 (95% CI: 0.9471-0.9774). Using the pre-determined threshold, sensitivity was 92.9% and specificity 87.9%, yielding a positive LR of 7.65 and negative LR of 0.08. Model-derived probabilities showed strong associations with echocardiographic measures of AS severity (adjusted R2 = 0.5051 for peak transvalvular velocity). Exploratory subgroup analyses showed generally consistent performance, although estimates were imprecise in small subgroups.
The eAS model demonstrated high diagnostic performance for detecting moderate-or-greater AS in a multicenter external validation cohort. AI-based PCG/ECG analysis may support the decision to refer patients from auscultation to echocardiography for AS evaluation.

title: Stent biomechanics in hemodialysis-related left brachiocephalic vein stenosis: from site-specific loading to a staged device-validation framework.
authors: Shanyuan Jin; Chuhan Chen; Guiye Na; Lin Guo; Li Dai; Bing Liu
abstract: Hemodialysis-related left brachiocephalic vein stenosis is usually managed as one local variant of central venous stenosis, yet its mechanical environment is distinctive. The vein follows a long, multi-axially curved retrosternal course through a narrow window between the manubrium and the aortic arch, bounded by two separate junctions, the lateral venous angle and the medial brachiocephalic-caval confluence. An implanted stent is therefore exposed to focal unidirectional compression, cyclic bending and torsion, short landing zones, and branch-coverage risk, conditions not reproduced by circumferential radial testing. The sternum-aortic corridor reported in affected patients, about 4.6 mm, is narrower than the nominal diameter of stents deployed there, placing the implied compression at or beyond the lowest level characterized in published bench comparisons; pulsatile durability testing covers only cardiac-frequency diametric cycling, and pooled cohorts seldom report the segment separately. This Review synthesizes published anatomical, clinical, engineering, and computational evidence and reframes the problem as a site-specific biomechanical and device-validation question with three validation priority stages (P1-P3). P1 (required) evaluates base-platform mechanics, structure, fatigue, and deployment: focal crush resistance and recovery, radial resistive versus chronic outward force, bending and torsion durability, foreshortening, deployment accuracy, branch preservation and, for covered constructs, covering fatigue. P2 (required) evaluates anatomy-specific hemodynamics of the same platform by patient-specific computational modeling and experimental flow testing, reporting shear, residence, gradient, edge-recirculation, branch-flow, and pressure-loss metrics against matched comparators. P3 (optional) covers an added drug, coating, or surface; baseline thrombogenicity, hemocompatibility, tissue compatibility, and structural integrity remain required base-platform attributes. We state two falsifiable hypotheses with the bench, computational, imaging, and clinical evidence that would support or refute them: H1 (mechanical), that resistance to focal unidirectional crush may govern stent deformation, durability, and in-stent restenosis localization more strongly than circumferential radial resistive force alone; and H2 (hemodynamic), that stent architecture and edge configuration may generate spatially reproducible disturbed-flow regions adding incremental prediction of later in-stent restenosis distribution beyond anatomical and procedural covariates. Direct prospective evidence remains sparse: the framework is a problem definition and validation roadmap, not a clinical algorithm, device ranking, or evidence of superior performance.

title: Modified balloon-assisted shoehorn technique for transcatheter aortic valve implantation in functionally horizontal anatomy: a case report.
authors: Nilkanth Patil; Rajeev Menon; Uday Kiran Anne; Pragathi Gurram; Anuj Kapadiya
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) in bicuspid aortic valve (BAV) poses unique challenges. We report a case in which an apparently benign anatomy resulted in failure of conventional delivery strategies and required a novel balloon-assisted bailout technique.
A 59-year-old man with a background history of liver cirrhosis presented with severe aortic stenosis due to type 1 BAV. The patient was in Child-Pugh class A with model for end-stage liver disease (MELD) score of 14; hence, he was planned for TAVI in view of high surgical risk. Pre-procedural computed tomography showed a favourable left ventricular (LV)-aortic angle, but the fused non-coronary and right-coronary cusp behaved like functional horizontal anatomy. Various previously described wire and balloon-assisted techniques failed to deliver the valve. A novel balloon-assisted modified 'shoe-horn' technique, by inflating a 16 mm balloon in non-coronary sinus, altered the delivery trajectory and enabled successful valve delivery.
BAV with right non-coronary cusps fusion may behave like horizontal anatomy, despite favourable LV-aortic angle. A modified balloon-assisted shoe-horn technique can facilitate valve delivery when conventional methods fail. This case highlights an under-recognized mechanism of valve delivery failure in BAV and emphasizes the importance of preparedness for advanced bailout strategies.

title: Impaired Flow and Physiology in Coronaries With Anomalous Origin From the Opposite Sinus of Valsalva.
authors: Mauro Lo Rito; Mattia Squillace; Mauro Luca Agnifili; Antonio Rosato; Serena Anglese; Adele Chiavetta; Camilla Muritti; Miriam Deamici; Jessica Negri; Andrea Attanasio; Gianluigi Guida; Giandomenico Disabato; Francesco Secchi; Michele Conti; Alessandro Frigiola; Massimo Chessa; Alessandro Giamberti; Francesco Bedogni
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Anomalous Aortic Origin of a Coronary Artery (AAOCA) high-risk anatomical features (intramural segment, acute take-off angle, slit-like ostium) cause coronary stenosis leading to myocardial infarction. How these features alter coronary physiology remains unclear.
We aimed to evaluate their impact on coronary blood supply using continuous thermodilution.
We prospectively enrolled 51 AAOCA patients undergoing continuous thermodilution. Subjects were classified into an ischemic risk (IR) group (intramural segment, acute angle, oval or slit ostium) or non-ischemic risk (no-IR) group. Non-anomalous coronary arteries served as controls. We measured absolute coronary blood flow (CBF) and microvascular resistance.
Subjects (median age 48.4 years) presented mostly with angina, syncope, and arrhythmia. Final analysis included 48 AAOCA cases (31 IR, 17 no-IR) and 45 controls. The IR group had a median IM length of 9 mm, take-off angle of 31.9°, and a slit-like or oval ostium. The no-IR group had a median angle of 51.5° and an oval or round ostium. At rest, absolute CBF and microvascular resistance showed no significant differences among groups. However, during hyperemia, the IR group had significantly reduced CBF compared to controls (179 vs. 290 mL/min, p = 0.015). The IR group demonstrated higher microvascular resistance at rest (1473 vs. 1150, p = 0.024) and during hyperemia (433 vs. 305, p = 0.012), indicating persistently increased coronary vascular tone.
High-risk anatomical features of AAOCA are associated with altered coronary physiology. An intramural segment, acute take-off angle, and slit-like or oval ostium are linked to reduced hyperemic coronary blood flow due to increased microvascular resistance.

title: Pre-Procedural Prediction of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Normalization After Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation.
authors: Yuki Hida; Teruhiko Imamura; Hiroshi Ueno; Koichiro Kinugawa; Masanori Yamamoto; Takahiro Tokuda; Tetsuro Shimura; Shinichi Shirai; Kenichi Ishizu; Yohei Ohno; Fumiaki Yashima; Toru Naganuma; Yusuke Watanabe; Futoshi Yamanaka; Gaku Nakazawa; Masahiko Noguchi; Masaki Izumo; Masahiko Asami; Hidetaka Nishina; Hiroto Suzuyama; Kazumasa Yamasaki; Kenji Nishioka; Daisuke Hachinohe; Yasushi Fuku; Toshiaki Otsuka; Kentaro Hayashida; OCEAN‐TAVI Investigators
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract:
Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) is an established therapy for severe aortic stenosis. Among patients with left ventricular (LV) systolic dysfunction, recovery of LV function after TAVI is heterogeneous, and reliable tools for pre-procedural risk stratification and patient counseling remain limited.
We sought to identify simple pre-procedural predictors of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI and to develop a clinically applicable risk score to support patient counseling and post-procedural management.
We retrospectively analyzed patients with severe aortic stenosis and baseline LV ejection fraction (LVEF) < 40% enrolled in a large multicenter registry in Japan. The primary outcome was complete LVEF normalization (LVEF > 50%) at 1 year after TAVI. Independent predictors were identified using multivariable logistic regression in a derivation cohort, and an exploratory weighted score was constructed. The score was preliminarily assessed in a separate single-center cohort.
The derivation cohort comprised 177 patients (median age 84 years; 44% women), of whom 94 (53%) achieved LVEF normalization. Lower body mass index (odds ratio [OR] 0.86, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.77-0.95; p = 0.004), higher aortic valve peak velocity (OR 2.45, 95% CI 1.40-4.29; p = 0.002), and smaller LV end-diastolic diameter (OR 0.93, 95% CI 0.88-0.98; p = 0.020) were independently associated with LVEF normalization. The derived score stratified patients into low-, intermediate-, and high-probability groups (15%, 45%, and 71%, respectively; p < 0.001), with consistent discrimination in the validation cohort.
A simple exploratory score incorporating body mass index, transvalvular peak velocity, and LV size was associated with the probability of complete LV functional recovery after TAVI. This pre-procedural tool may facilitate patient counseling, expectation-setting, and identification of patients who may require closer heart failure follow-up after TAVI. It should not be used to determine eligibility for TAVI.

title: Short-Term Complications of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis (PROLONG-TAVR).
authors: Mauricio Castillo-Perez; Humberto De León-Gutiérrez; Carlos Jerjes-Sánchez; Lillian Royzman-Rivera; Jose Gildardo Paredes-Vazquez; Vicente Jimenez-Franco; Paola Gutiérrez-Gallegos; Maria J Cabada-Garcia; Jahir Rodriguez-Rivera; Enrique Paredes-Gutierrez; Renata Quevedo-Salazar; Juan F Sanchez-Avila
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
abstract: To estimate the cumulative incidence of short-term complications across different transcatheter heart valve (THV) prostheses used for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). We performed a systematic review and meta-analysis in accordance with PRISMA and a prospectively registered PROSPERO protocol. Observational studies published from 2002 through May 2024 that included patients with severe aortic stenosis undergoing predominantly transfemoral TAVR and reported prosthesis-specific complications were eligible. Although the original protocol intended to evaluate both short- and long-term complications, long-term outcomes were too sparse and inconsistently reported for robust pooled analyses; therefore, the present analysis focuses on short-term complications. Pooled cumulative incidences were calculated using random-effects models. We included 242 studies comprising 181,187 patients. SAPIEN 3 had the lowest incidence of moderate-to-severe paravalvular leak (PVL) (1.04%, 95% CI 0.69-1.55) and stroke (1.87%, 95% CI 1.64-2.14), whereas ACURATE neo2 had the lowest incidence of permanent pacemaker implantation (PPI) (7.7%, 95% CI 5.82-10.11). Evolut PRO and SAPIEN 3 showed among the lowest rates of major vascular complications (3.56%, 95% CI 2.77-4.57 and 3.87%, 95% CI 3.22-4.66, respectively) and major or life-threatening bleeding (2.96%, 95% CI 2.09-4.17 and 4.8%, 95% CI 4.04-5.69, respectively). Short-term complications have decreased with newer-generation THV prostheses. PVL remains more frequent with self-expanding valves, whereas PPI is the most frequent complication and is generally less frequent with balloon-expandable valves and ACURATE neo2. Stroke rates have changed little across newer generations, and annular rupture, coronary artery obstruction, and valve embolization remain rare (< 1%).

title: It Is Possible to Save the Kidney With Renal Artery Occlusion Without Autotransplantation: A Case Report.
authors: Adem Şafak; Emre Karakaya; İlgin Demir; Esra Baskın; Sedat Yıldırım; Atilla Sezgin; Mehmet Haberal
abstract: Renal artery stenosis is a rare but important cause of renovascular hypertension in children that may lead to malignant hypertension and renal failure. A 13-year-old girl presented with malignant hypertension and acute kidney injury, and imaging demonstrated occlusion of both renal arteries. Endovascular recanalization was unsuccessful because of complete, heavily fibrotic occlusions involving a long segment of the right renal artery extending to the hilum, leaving no suitable distal artery for reconstruction, and a 7.3-mm segment of the left renal artery at its aortic origin. To preserve renal function, surgical revascularization was performed by in situ reimplantation of the left renal artery into the aorta, without autotransplantation. Postoperatively, renal function recovered, the proteinuria present at admission regressed, and the patient became normotensive without antihypertensive medication.

title: Exploratory Analysis of the Innate Immune System in Aortic Stenosis Patients With and Without ASCVD.
authors: Amber van Broekhoven; Eveline P M van Doorn; Wieteke Broeders; Aysun Cetinyurek-Yavuz; Erwin S Zegers; Mihai G Netea; Alexander B A Vonk; Niels van Royen; Hans W M Niessen; Jan H Cornel; Niels P Riksen; Saloua El Messaoudi
abstract: Calcific aortic valve disease (CAVD) leads to aortic stenosis (AS) through inflammation and fibro-calcific remodeling. Although CAVD and atherosclerosis share features, not all patients with AS develop atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD), suggesting mechanistic heterogeneity. This case-control study evaluated inflammatory profiles and valvular remodeling in 128 patients with AS (59.4% with ASCVD) and 105 controls. Immune cell composition and monocyte markers were analyzed by flow cytometry, whereas cytokine production was assessed after peripheral blood mononuclear cell (PBMC) stimulation. Both AS groups had higher interleukin (IL)-6, leukocyte, monocyte, and neutrophil counts than controls, with lower monocyte human leukocyte antigen-DR isotype and higher C-C chemokine receptor (CCR)2 expression. Cytokine responses were also elevated, particularly in AS patients with ASCVD. They also showed higher IL-6 concentrations, higher proportions of classical monocytes, and lower intermediate and non-classical monocytes compared with patients without ASCVD. Overall, AS was associated with a pro-inflammatory monocyte phenotype and function, most prominently in patients with ASCVD. ClinicalTrials.gov ID: NCT04717219.

title: A Proactive Digital Valve Care Pathway for Management of Severe Aortic Stenosis: The DETECT AS II Study.
authors: Seyed Mohammad Forouzannia; Jassmine Hempstead; Katherine Steineman; Rong Duan; Patrick Vossler; Jean Feng; Siyu Zhou; Lucas S Zier; Sammy Elmariah

title: AI-Based Wound Measurement in a Telemedicine-Style Workflow: Agreement With In-Person Reference Measurements Compared With Individual Physicians and Expert Consensus.
authors: Tassilo Dege; Vanessa Borst; Luisa Deutzmann; Jan Hendrik Maiwald; Samuel Kounev; Astrid Schmieder
abstract: Accurate wound size measurement is essential for monitoring healing, yet visual estimates are variable-especially in telemedicine-style assessments. To compare AI-based wound size estimates with physician image-based estimates using in-person measurements as ground truth (GT). In a prospective dataset of bedside wound photographs (Dec 2024-Apr 2025), GT height and width were measured in person by two experienced raters using a calibrated ruler. A set of ArUco markers placed adjacent to the wound at the same skin level enabled image-based retrieval of real-world size information. Five physicians estimated height and width from images in a telemedicine-style workflow. Two deep-learning segmentation architectures (TransNeXt-Tiny [TransNeXt] and VWFormerConvNeXtS [VW-Conv]) generated automated size estimates. Agreement and error were quantified using ICC(2,1), Pearson's r, MAE, bias and Bland-Altman limits of agreement. In addition, pixel-level segmentation performance of both models was quantified against expert-annotated reference masks using Intersection-over-Union (IoU), the Dice coefficient, precision and recall, reported as macro-averaged (per-image) and micro-averaged (pixel-pooled) values. AI achieved excellent agreement for height (TransNeXt ICC = 0.96, MAE = 0.82 cm; VW-Conv ICC = 0.95, MAE = 0.68 cm) with minimal bias. For width, AI showed moderate-to-strong agreement with a tendency to underestimation (TransNeXt ICC = 0.86, MAE = 0.69 cm, bias = -0.42 cm; VW-Conv ICC = 0.77, MAE = 0.74 cm, bias = -0.64 cm). Individual physician performance was heterogeneous, while a human consensus improved agreement (height ICC = 0.94, MAE = 0.82 cm; width ICC = 0.91, MAE = 0.65 cm). At the pixel level, TransNeXt reached a macro-averaged Dice of 0.886 (IoU 0.805) and VW-Conv a macro-averaged Dice of 0.818 (IoU 0.733), with TransNeXt showing the more consistent per-image performance. AI-based wound measurement was more consistent than single physician estimates and reached agreement comparable to, but not exceeding, a consensus of experts. Within the constraints of this single-centre validation study, these findings support AI-assisted measurement as an objective aid for standardised wound monitoring in telemedicine and clinical research; confirmation in larger, multicentre and prospectively recruited cohorts is required.

title: A Retrospective Benchmark of Quantitative Antimicrobial Peptide Activity Prediction Tools.
authors: Jianda Yue; Zhaoyang Tang; Xie Li; Jiawei Xu; Hua Tan; Qizhang Yang; Zhonghua Liu; Ying Wang
abstract: Antimicrobial peptides (AMPs) are critical candidates for addressing the global antibiotic resistance crisis. AI-driven quantitative models capable of directly predicting peptide antimicrobial activity, specifically minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC), are gaining scientific prominence by providing precise guidance for the rational design of AMPs. To assess their real-world, out-of-the-box performance, we conducted a retrospective benchmark of 10 publicly released quantitative AMP prediction tools spanning classical machine learning and contemporary deep learning approaches. Using an external dataset and reconstructed native datasets, we evaluated absolute MIC regression, retrospective reproducibility, directional prediction patterns, ranking capability, and virtual-screening enrichment. Most released tools exhibited poor absolute MIC regression and limited transferability to the external benchmark, while selected tools retained useful relative-ranking and enrichment capabilities. Retrospective evaluation further revealed marked differences in implementation-level reproducibility among the released tools. Error-stratified analyses identified systematic associations between prediction errors and peptide residue composition, together with a general compression of the predicted activity range. Collectively, these findings characterize the practical performance boundaries of currently accessible quantitative AMP prediction tools and support their use primarily as early-stage screening filters rather than precise substitutes for experimental MIC measurements.

title: Machine Learning in Dementia Research: Trends, Biomarkers, Prediction Goals, and Data Modalities.
authors: Yao-Chin Wang; Hsien Chang Yeh; Md Mohaimenul Islam; Woon-Man Kung
abstract:
Machine learning (ML) is increasingly used in dementia research for diagnosis, early detection, prognosis, biomarker characterization, and disease phenotyping. This study aimed to provide a bibliometric and thematic overview of ML applications in dementia, emphasizing biological mechanisms, prediction goals, data modalities, collaborative networks, and emerging computational approaches.
A title-field search of the Web of Science Core Collection identified 3,833 records related to ML and dementia. After restricting publications to 2000 onward and excluding non-analytic document types, 3,479 records were included in the bibliometric analysis. A subset of 3,223 original articles was used for thematic analyses. Publication trends, authorship, institutional collaboration, keywords, biomarker themes, ML objectives, data modalities, methods, shared research resources, and large language model (LLM) applications were evaluated.
ML-related dementia research increased substantially over time. Diagnostic classification was the predominant ML objective (55.0%), followed by early detection or screening (10.3%), progression or cognitive-decline prediction (6.8%), and biomarker or feature discovery (4.7%). Structural magnetic resonance imaging was the most frequently identified modality (42.6%), followed by clinical or cognitive data (22.4%), positron emission tomography/single photon emission computerized tomography (10.3%), and genetic or genomic data (10.2%). Prominent biological themes included hippocampal measures, amyloid/Aβ, electroencephalogram, tau/p-tau, and cerebrospinal fluid biomarkers. Institutional networks showed distinct international collaboration clusters and frequent use of shared infrastructures. Transformer-based and LLM approaches emerged in recent years.
ML research in dementia has expanded beyond diagnostic neuroimaging toward multimodal, biomarker, prognostic, and language model applications, although diagnostic classification and structural imaging remain dominant. Emphasis on biological integration, longitudinal validation, and clinical translation are needed.

title: Advancing Cancer Biomarker Discovery Through Multi-Omics, Bioinformatics, and Artificial Intelligence: A Systematic Review.
authors: Pendy Tok; Vijayan Manickam-Achari; Siow-Wee Chang
abstract: The rapid accumulation of multi-omics data provides increasing opportunities for cancer biomarker discovery, but the heterogeneity and high dimensionality of these datasets remain major challenges for data integration and analysis. This review examines the application of bioinformatics and artificial intelligence for multi-omics integration in cancer biomarker research. Common multi-omics data paradigms and integration strategies are discussed, followed by a review of the bioinformatics, machine learning and deep learning approaches applied across 84 included studies. Cross-study comparison showed limited recurrence among the reported biomarkers, with only 15 biomarkers identified in at least four studies. Further assessment of the 13 recurrent protein-coding biomarkers showed significant protein-protein interaction enrichment and functional convergence in cancer-related processes, particularly PI3K/AKT and ERBB2-related signaling. This review also highlights current challenges, including missing data, heterogeneity across datasets, limited independent validation and the interpretability of artificial intelligence models. Future research may benefit from integrating multi-omics data with clinical information, pathological imaging, electronic health records, single-cell multi-omics and radiomics, together with broader datasets and greater use of independent validation to support the translation of multi-omics biomarker findings into clinical applications.

title: Artificial Intelligence Applications for Composite Materials: A Review.
authors: Nada S Alharthi; Laila M Alqahtani; Albatool A Abaalkhail; Ibtehal S Baazeem; Mustafa Y Haddad; Mohammed T Alamoudi; Basheer A Alshammari
abstract:
Composite materials are not easy to model using traditional experiments and physics-based approaches due to their diverse properties and multiscale nature. This review summarizes how artificial intelligence (AI) methodologies, including machine learning, deep learning, and generative AI, have been increasingly transforming and how they have been increasingly applied to composite materials research. It combines their possible use across the prediction of their properties, damage detection, structural health monitoring, and materials design.
Searches were performed in Scopus and Google Scholar for articles published using combined keywords such as "(artificial intelligence OR machine learning OR deep learning OR Generative AI) AND (composite OR fiber reinforced) AND (prediction OR optimization OR characterization)". The search strategy was designed to capture both fundamental developments in AI methodologies relevant to materials research and their specific applications to composite materials. The identified publications underwent a two-step selection process: (i) an initial review of titles and abstracts, and (ii) a detailed full-text evaluation. Studies were included if they provided explicit descriptions of AI models, clearly specified datasets, and applied quantitative performance assessments to composite materials-related applications such as material property prediction, damage detection, characterization, or manufacturing process optimization. For each selected article, relevant information was extracted in a structured and consistent manner, including the type of composite material, AI methodology, input parameters, dataset characteristics and size, validation methods, and application domain. These data were used to support both quantitative trend analysis and the qualitative identification of research gaps and future research opportunities in composite materials research.
Supervised learning methods, in particular artificial neural networks, support vector machines, random forests, and decision trees, were commonly used and exhibited durable potential accuracy in predicting properties of composite materials. Unsupervised methods such as principal component analysis (PCA) and clustering were comparatively underused. Generative AI, including generative adversarial networks (GANs) and variational autoencoders (VAEs), and physics-informed models emerged as growing approaches for synthetic data generation and improved interpretability, respectively.
The reviewed studies were frequently limited by small or heterogeneous datasets, weak generalizability testing beyond training conditions, high computational requirements and limited model interpretability ("black box" behavior); a risk-of-bias assessment across included studies was not formally conducted.
AI is shifting composite materials research from trial-and-error toward data-driven, predictive design. Realizing its full potential will require open, well-annotated datasets, physics-aware and explainable models, and closed-loop, active-learning workflows linking prediction to experimental validation.

title: Aerial Phenotyping of Coffee Flowering Using Deep Learning for Early Yield Prediction.
authors: Elias Horácio Zavala; Gabriel Araújo E Silva Ferraz; Felipe Andrés Obando Vega; Mirian de Lourdes Oliveira; Milene Alves de Figueiredo Carvalho; Samuel Henrique Braga da Cunha; Andrea Pagliai; Daniele Sarri
abstract: Early yield estimation is important for improving decision-making and management practices in coffee production systems. However, approaches that use aerial imagery to characterize flowering and relate it to subsequent yield remain limited. This study evaluated the potential of RGB imagery acquired by remotely piloted aircraft (RPA) combined with Deep Learning techniques to classify coffee plants according to three levels of a flowering proxy and to investigate its relationship with yield. A dataset comprising 1593 segmented RGB images was classified into Low, Medium, and High flowering levels using a custom convolutional neural network and three transfer learning architectures: VGG16, ResNet50V2, and MobileNetV2. ResNet50V2 was selected for final evaluation based on its validation performance and achieved 92.12% accuracy, 92.40% macro-precision, 91.81% macro-recall, and 92.06% macro-F1 on the test dataset. The flowering proxy showed a positive association with field-observed yield, with Spearman's ρ = 0.701 (p < 0.001) and R2 = 0.528 for the combined dataset of Arara and Mundo Novo. In consolidated out-of-sample predictions, the model achieved R2 = 0.489, MAE = 1.03 kg plant-1, and RMSE = 1.18 kg plant-1. Performance differed between cultivars, with consolidated R2 values of 0.567 for Arara and 0.329 for Mundo Novo. Spatial analysis also showed correspondence between the distribution of flowering levels derived from RGB imagery and the subsequent spatial distribution of yield. These findings indicate that RPA-based RGB imagery and Deep Learning can provide spatialized information related to coffee flowering and its productive performance, with potential applications in precision agriculture. Further evaluation across production cycles, cultivars, and environmental conditions is needed to assess the robustness and generalization of the approach.

title: Internal Consistency Does Not Validate an LLM-Assisted Nutrition Pipeline: A Reference-Standard-Free Forensic Reliability Audit of 13,073 Free-Text Meal Records.
authors: Jhony Fernando López Torres; Juan Gabriel Castañeda; Edwin Rivas
abstract:
Large language model (LLM) pipelines increasingly convert free-text meal descriptions into nutrient values, yet reference-standard validation is rarely feasible in production. We asked whether the controls such pipelines conventionally pass suffice and built a reference-standard-free battery any pipeline can run on its output.
We audited 13,073 meals logged by 513 adults through a WhatsApp conversational agent in rural Colombia (9 February 2026 to 6 August 2026). The pipeline is a two-stage cascade of commercial LLMs from different providers: a vision model renders photographs as text, while a text model maps these to nutrients. Six pre-specified tests were applied, including test-retest ICC(1,1) over recurring strings, stratified by modality because 48.3% of records carried a photograph.
The pipeline passed every conventional control (Atwater-reconstructed energy r = 0.9951; median relative error 0.0000) but failed reproducibility. Across 191 recurring strings (944 meals), energy ICC point estimates were 0.7061 (95% CI 0.5419-0.8217) text only and 0.5258 (0.3778-0.6513) with photographs; none reached 0.75. Modality is a design control, not an established effect, and the coefficient depends on which inputs recur, so it is not intrinsic. Under the strictest identity available-byte-identical text, no photograph-ICC was 0.6944. Intermediate-text inspection exposed a failure invisible at the output: 1.44% of photograph-accompanied records carried a vision-stage artefact string versus 0.01% of text-only records (ICC 0.0911).
Internal consistency does not validate an LLM-assisted nutrition pipeline. This design measures instability under recurring inputs without isolating its cause. Prospective test-retest reproducibility is a cheap, necessary acceptance criterion, and in a cascade, the intermediate representation must also be inspected.

title: From Genes to Diets: A Critical Review of Genetic, Nutrigenomic and Epigenetic Mechanisms in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus.
authors: Rafael G Araújo; Gabriela Ortiz-Cruz; Sunday Sedodo Nupo; Yulianna Cordero; Lauro Cortes-Hernandez; Sandra Lucía Teniente
abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2D) represents over 90% of diabetes cases globally, posing a growing public health crisis with an estimated 783 million adults projected to be affected by 2045. This condition arises from a complex interplay of insulin resistance, progressive pancreatic β-cell dysfunction, and chronic low-grade inflammation, strongly influenced by genetic predisposition, obesity, sedentary lifestyle, and poor dietary habits. While genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified key susceptibility loci, including TCF7L2, PPARG, and KCNJ11, these varian0ts explain only ~10% of T2D heritability, underscoring the critical role of gene-environment interactions. This review synthesizes current evidence on the genetic, nutrigenomic, and epigenetic mechanisms underlying T2D pathogenesis and progression. We examine how dietary components, such as flavonoids, terpenoids, alkaloids, and bioactive compounds from natural products, modulate gene expression via transcription factors and influence insulin sensitivity, oxidative stress, and inflammation. Furthermore, we explore the emerging role of epigenetic modifications, including DNA methylation, histone acetylation, and chromatin remodeling, in mediating the lasting effects of hyperglycemia and environmental factors on T2D risk. The potential of epigenetic biomarkers for early diagnosis, patient stratification, and personalized therapy is discussed. Finally, we highlight how next-generation sequencing and artificial intelligence, particularly machine learning and deep learning models, are advancing multi-omics data integration, enabling improved T2D subtype classification, prognosis prediction, and the development of precision nutrition and pharmacoepigenetic strategies.

title: Nutrient Calculation Accuracy, Expert-Rated Clinical Appropriateness and Safety Indicators, and Reproducibility of Large Language Model-Generated Diet Plans for Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome: A Real-Case-Based Evaluation.
authors: Ayşenur Çalık; Pınar Ece Demiray; Ayşe Betül Bilen; Gülen Ecem Kalkan; Muazzez Garipağaoğlu
abstract: Background/Objectives: This study evaluated the nutrient calculation accuracy, reproducibility, and expert-rated clinical appropriateness and safety indicators of three-day diet plans generated for women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), recently proposed to be termed polyendocrine metabolic ovarian syndrome (PMOS). Methods: Anonymized data from six women with heterogeneous PMOS profiles, purposively selected from a single clinic, were converted into standardized Turkish prompts and submitted to ChatGPT-4, Claude Sonnet 4.6, Gemini 2.5 Flash, and Mistral 2.0 through free web interfaces. Three independent generations per case-model combination yielded 216 daily menus. LLM-reported nutrient values were compared with BeBiS 9.0 calculations. Reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs). Two experts independently evaluated the first generated plan for each case-model combination using a study-specific clinical appropriateness rubric and red-flag checklist. Results: No model achieved consistently low error across nutrients. Claude Sonnet 4.6 showed the lowest percentage errors for energy, carbohydrate, and fiber; ChatGPT-4 for protein; and Mistral 2.0 for fat. Gemini 2.5 Flash showed the largest percentage errors across all nutrients and a mean energy bias of +531.1 kcal. ChatGPT-4 showed comparatively higher plan-level reproducibility, while the remaining models generally showed poor reproducibility. Claude Sonnet 4.6 had the highest descriptive clinical appropriateness scores and Gemini 2.5 Flash the lowest, but no pairwise differences remained significant after Holm correction. Gemini 2.5 Flash generated the most confirmed study-specific red flags (n = 28), with all six cases meeting the criterion for the "masked low-energy" indicator. Conclusions: LLM-generated diet plans showed model-dependent calculation errors and limited reproducibility, and the present findings do not support their independent or unsupervised use as individualized clinical nutrition recommendations.

title: Developing a Machine Learning-Based System for Nutrient Profiling of Pakistani Cuisine.
authors: Alishba Umer Farooq; Fiza Khan; Huda Ijaz; Muhammad Usman; Nimra Saleem; Shuja Ur Rehman Baig; Muhammad Farooq; Syed Mustafa Ali
abstract:
Chronic diseases such as diabetes and heart disease are rising in South Asia, with poor diet a major contributor. Most dietary apps are designed for Western foods and struggle with culturally diverse dishes such as Pakistani cuisine.
This study aimed to build a machine learning-based system that can recognise Pakistani dishes, estimate portion sizes, and calculate their nutritional value.
We developed a multi-stage automated dietary assessment pipeline for Pakistani cuisine using a multi-source dataset covering 83 dish classes across 10 categories. Following data cleaning, class balancing, and targeted augmentation, deep learning architectures were evaluated for food classification and segmentation. ResNet-50, MobileNetV2, and YOLOv8 were used for food recognition, while YOLOv8-Seg and Mask R-CNN enabled pixel-level segmentation for portion and nutrient estimation. All models were optimized using transfer learning and evaluated using standard classification and mask-quality metrics, followed by mobile application usability testing.
A multi-source dataset of ten categories and 83 Pakistani dishes was used to train and compare deep learning models for food classification and segmentation. Portion size was estimated using a segmentation- and depth-based approach without a reference object, while nutritional values were derived from standardised recipes and established food databases. The models were integrated into a mobile application for usability testing. YOLO-based models achieved the best balance of accuracy and speed for real-time classification and segmentation. Portion estimates were reasonably close to measured values, and usability testing showed the app was easy to use, with minor improvements suggested.
Overall, this work demonstrates the feasibility of an AI-based dietary assessment system adapted to Pakistani cuisine, with future work focused on reducing processing demands and improving depth-based portion estimation.

title: Nutritional Accuracy and Clinical Applicability of Large Language Model-Generated Therapeutic Diet Plans for Phenylketonuria: A Comparative Simulation Study.
authors: Bahar Kulu; Banu Süzen; Nuriye Ece Mintaş; Sibel Burçak Şahin Uyar; Esra Özcan; Fulya Durğun; Neslihan Buse Tatlıdil; Nur Arslan; Volkan Hancı
abstract: Background: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate nutrition-related recommendations, but their reliability for therapeutic diets requiring precise nutrient control remains uncertain. This study evaluated AI-generated one-day diet plans for standardized simulated cases of classical phenylketonuria (PKU). Methods: Eight standardized simulated cases representing infancy, adolescence, adulthood, and maternal PKU were evaluated. Between 8 and 10 February 2026, ChatGPT-5.2, Claude 4.5, and Gemini 3 were each used through their standard consumer-facing chat interfaces to generate one diet plan per case under two prompting conditions, yielding 48 plans. Nutrient composition was independently recalculated using BİAYS, and three blinded pediatric metabolic dietitians evaluated the plans using a structured 25-item checklist. Results: Across all 48 plans, phenylalanine provision calculated using BİAYS was below the case-specific prescription in 36 plans (75.0%). After Holm correction, none of the 12 paired AI-reported versus BİAYS-calculated nutrient comparisons remained statistically significant, while plan-level error metrics demonstrated substantial variability for several nutrients. Overall expert scores did not differ among models, whereas clinically specified structured prompts received higher expert ratings than limited-information zero-shot prompts. Inter-rater reliability was modest at the diet-plan level. Conclusions: AI-generated PKU diet plans may incorporate core dietary principles, but numerical plausibility does not ensure agreement with independent nutrient calculations or adherence to individualized clinical prescriptions. Independent nutrient verification and specialist metabolic-dietitian review remain necessary. Because only one output was generated for each case-model-prompt combination, the findings characterize the 48 evaluated outputs rather than within-model reproducibility.

title: When the Algorithm Becomes the Dietitian: Large Language Model Hallucinations, Algorithmic Food Environments, and the Erosion of Nutritional Autonomy.
authors: Ismail Dergaa; Rym Ben Othman; Hatem Ghouili; Halil İbrahim Ceylan; Nizar Souissi; Souhail Bchini; Valentina Stefanica; Raul Ioan Muntean; Nicola Luigi Bragazzi
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can answer dietary questions, but their use as substitutes for registered dietitians remains insufficiently quantified. Evaluations have identified inaccurate nutrient targets, incomplete clinical advice, and insufficient personalization, alongside useful performance on some general nutrition tasks. Social media and food-delivery interfaces may also influence dietary choices through food cues, social endorsement, and choice architecture. This conceptual perspective presents ADRIFT (Algorithmic Dietary Reconfiguration through Informational, Framing, and Technological mechanisms) to examine how these influences might interact. Drawing on a targeted, nonsystematic synthesis of nutrition, behavioral, neuroscience, and AI literature, ADRIFT distinguishes three axes: informational errors and unsupported advice; framing through content and interface design; and adaptive personalization and cognitive delegation. Direct evidence supports selected component mechanisms, but their convergence into a feedback loop that reduces nutritional autonomy remains hypothetical. We propose a six-category taxonomy covering hallucinations and related nutrition errors, define nutritional autonomy erosion as declining capacity for informed, self-directed dietary decisions, and outline eight testable hypotheses. The framework concerns unsupervised use and does not predict that language models will replace dietetic professionals. Longitudinal validation, platform experiments, and clinical safety evaluations are needed to determine whether, for whom, and under which conditions the proposed harms occur.

title: Advances in Deep Learning Models for Ground Deformation Prediction Using InSAR Approach: A Systematic Review with Special Emphasis on Subsidence as a Geo-Environmental Hazard.
authors: Nitish Kumar; Mohammad Soyeb Alam
abstract: Ground deformation, especially subsidence, is a geo-environmental hazard that needs to be assessed and predicted in advance to mitigate its effects efficiently and in a timely manner. Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR) provides high-resolution, all-weather ground deformation monitoring, while advances in Deep Learning (DL) have significantly improved its analytical capabilities. Despite growing interest in integrating DL with InSAR, existing systematic reviews have focused mainly on urban infrastructure, leaving mining-induced subsidence comparatively underexplored. This review addresses this gap by applying the PRISMA framework to systematically evaluate 162 peer-reviewed studies, including 21 core articles on DL-based mining subsidence and 58 supporting studies from related deformation applications. This paper examines DL architectures, including CNNs, LSTMs, GRUs, ConvLSTMs, Transformers, and Graph Neural Networks, and assesses their roles in data decomposition, spatiotemporal feature extraction, hyperparameter optimization, and multi-source data fusion. Comparative analysis of 71 models shows that attention-enhanced CNN-LSTM and ConvLSTM architectures consistently outperform single-model approaches. Key challenges include limited mining datasets, poor cross-site transferability, lack of standardized benchmarks, and insufficient geomechanical integration. Finally, we propose a seven-point research roadmap to support reliable, explainable, transferable, and operational early-warning systems for mining-induced subsidence monitoring.

title: Semi-Supervised Adversarial Graph Prediction Model for Industrial Assets.
authors: Weijie Kang; Yuze Wei; Junhao Wang; Chaoyin Ma; Bo Liu; Bing He; Guodong Duan
abstract: In the field of Prognostics and Health Management (PHM), deep learning methods have shown excellent remaining useful life (RUL) prediction ability because of their powerful data fitting ability. Such methods require a large amount of failure history to train, but for industrial assets, their life-cycle data are often insufficient, and effective repairs or replacements are frequently carried out before the failure occurs. On the one hand, these suspension history data cannot be directly used by traditional deep learning methods, resulting in the certain loss of degradation information. On the other hand, the internal structure of industrial assets and the types of features are complex and diverse. Traditional methods use Euclidean space to represent relevant data, ignoring the correlation between features. Therefore, we develop a semi-supervised adversarial graph prediction (SAGP) framework that combines adversarial learning, graph neural networks, and semi-supervised training, using both failure and suspension histories for RUL prediction. Based on graph neural networks, SAGP can effectively obtain the degradation information in the failure and suspension history by representing the degradation data in the form of graphs and setting multi-objective functions. Through semi-supervised learning, SAGP looks for failure and suspension histories similar to the current state and generates simulated data through adversarial training to improve the robustness of the model and finally achieve RUL prediction. Tool, engine, and bearing datasets are used to verify the accuracy and reliability of the SAGP model.

title: An Innovative Decoupled Spatio-Vertical-Temporal Learning Model Based on Topography Guidance for Wind Vector Forecasting.
authors: Xinyu Liu; Huan Li; Xinyue Mo
abstract: Accurate wind speed forecasting (WSF) is pivotal for the secure grid integration of wind farms and the optimization of power dispatching. However, the stochastic nature of atmospheric dynamics and their complex interactions with local terrain pose significant challenges. Traditional spatiotemporal models inherently suffer from severe homogenization, irreversibly destroying fine-grained aerodynamic textures and leading to cumulative directional errors over extended horizons. To dismantle these limitations, this study proposes a novel Topography-Guided Spatio-Vertical-Temporal Transformer (TG-SVTFormer) for the multi-step forecasting of zonal and meridional wind vectors. Specifically, a dual-stage topography-guided mechanism explicitly injects static geographical variables (elevation, slope, and roughness) into both the spatial encoding and microscopic decoding phases, imposing key physical constraints on aerodynamic friction. Furthermore, the architecture employs a structured decoupled learning paradigm: a re-engineered Mix-Transformer spatial encoder deliberately eliminates deep-stage downsampling in favor of dilated convolutions-drastically expanding the global receptive field while preserving the intrinsic meteorological textures. Subsequently, the temporal evolution hub explicitly decouples the vertical dimension, utilizing upper-air atmospheric states to guide the target surface layer via simulated vertical momentum transport. The experiments showed the accuracy of TG-SVTFormer in predicting the wind speed with mean absolute error of 0.71 m/s in 3 h, 0.85 m/s in 6 h, and 1.06 m/s in 12 h. Compared to five existing baseline WSF models, the proposed TG-SVTFormer model demonstrates superior performance in wind speed forecasting and, more importantly, offers a transferable and physics-informed framework that can be adapted to other terrain-complex regions and extended to related renewable-energy and air-quality forecasting tasks.

title: Scooter-Driving Humanoid Robot: Sim-to-Real Transfer Through Deep Reinforcement Learning.
authors: Ugo Richard Roux; Saeed Saeedvand; Jacky Baltes
abstract: This paper presents a simulation-to-reality (sim-to-real) transfer process, allowing a full-sized humanoid robot to autonomously balance a two-wheeled scooter and track operator-supplied heading commands through a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) policy, including while carrying a human passenger for the first time. The learned policy governs the coupled balance and steering dynamics only: the heading reference and the target speed are supplied by a human operator, the throttle is set externally, and the initial launch over the first 2 to 3 m and the final stop are performed manually for safety. The system therefore performs autonomous balance and steering-command tracking during motion, rather than autonomous scooter driving. Unlike four-wheeled vehicles where the inherent stability simplifies control, scooter operation demands continuous and precise dynamic balancing coupled with real-time steering control, creating a challenging full-body control task. In this study, we demonstrate a successful integration of DRL techniques to bridge the sim-to-real gap, achieving stable closed-loop control of a humanoid robot balancing and steering a scooter under significant model uncertainty.
