A multi-scenario real-world evaluation shows the system maintaining control in the demanding low-speed regime of 0.8 to 3.0 m s-1, where balance control is most challenging and where speed varied across the range during trials rather than being held at a set point. Success rates are 0.96 on straight-line driving, 0.92 and 0.72 on light and sharp turns, 0.88 on the traversal of a 60 mm speed bump, and 0.73 while carrying a 70 kg passenger. They fall where sustained precise tracking is required, to 0.28 on a 4.5 m roundabout and 0.33 on part of the standardized Taiwanese scooter license test.

title: A Human-Machine Interaction-Experience-Learning Algorithm for Integrated Lateral-Longitudinal Decision-Making and Control in Intelligent Connected Vehicles.
authors: Wenxuan Shen; Cunyue Yan; Zhaoqiang Wang; Zeng Huang; Wei Gao
abstract: Traditional reinforcement learning for autonomous driving faces challenges such as slow convergence, control instability, and limited adaptability. To address these issues, this paper proposes a hybrid decision-making framework that integrates V2X communication, human-machine interaction experience, and deep reinforcement learning. Based on the Actor-Critic architecture, the framework incorporates a human-like driving tendency network to constrain the policy search space and integrates a Kalman filter-based V2X communication anomaly handling module. The model constructs the vehicle's action space and state representation. Comparative experiments with a method lacking the driving tendency module and the hierarchical planning method DDPG-RRT* show that DDPG-HP achieves faster convergence and better scenario adaptability than these baselines. It effectively avoids static and dynamic obstacles, demonstrates anticipatory and gradual deceleration, and initiates braking 1.7 s earlier than the DDPG-RRT* method, thereby reducing collision risks and enhancing pedestrian safety. Furthermore, the communication anomaly compensation mechanism effectively improves the system's adaptability and overall robustness under unstable communication conditions.

title: An Artificial Intelligence Framework for Detection of Leukemia with Comparison Between Segmented and Non-Segmented Images.
authors: Rula Abdallat; Osama Al-Bataineh; Ali Mohammad Alqudah; Ausilah Alfraihat
abstract:
Accurate classification of Acute Lymphoblastic Leukemia (ALL) subtypes from peripheral blood smear (PBS) images using deep learning may support automated image-based analysis of this blood malignancy.
We developed a custom lightweight Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to classify white blood cells into four subtypes: Benign, Early Pre-B ALL, Pre-B ALL, and Pro-B ALL. We assessed performance using accuracy, ROC curves, and explainability techniques, including upsampled feature map activations, occlusion sensitivity, and SHAP-style explanation overlays, comparing original (Non-segmented) and HSV-Segmented images. To mitigate patient-level data leakage without explicit patient identifiers, we further used unsupervised K-means clustering of HSV color histograms to group 3256 images into 89 "proxy-patient" clusters. Consequently, we implemented rigorous subject-level grouped 5-fold cross-validation and Hold-Out protocols alongside standard image-level evaluations.
Under standard image-level evaluation, the model achieved 98.8% accuracy on non-segmented images and 91.3% on segmented images. Crucially, this performance advantage was maintained under strict subject-level cross-validation (97.9% vs. 89.7%), confirming the robustness of the findings against data leakage. Explainability visualizations demonstrated that HSV segmentation discarded vital contextual morphological cues, increasing confusion between closely related subtypes.
A lightweight CNN can accurately classify ALL subtypes directly from raw PBS images. The evaluated HSV segmentation degraded performance by removing contextual information. This study underscores the necessity of subject-level evaluation in medical imaging and indicates that mandatory preprocessing should be empirically justified rather than assumed beneficial.

title: Bayesian Variational Neural Architecture Search for Lightweight Weld Seam Feature Point Detection in Laser Vision Systems.
authors: Wenjia Mou; Yulin Wang; Chunyuan Liu; Yanbiao Zou
abstract: In laser vision-based robotic welding, the seam feature point must be located, under strong arc-light and spatter interference, in every frame acquired while the weld is being made, so that the torch can be steered in real time; the detector must therefore keep pace with the camera on the modest processor of an industrial controller. Conventional deep learning models encounter structural redundancy and high computational latency under this constraint. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a lightweight object detection model, whose box-center output is mapped to the weld seam feature point, optimized via Bayesian variational neural architecture search (BayeNAS), in which architecture parameters are modeled as Gaussian distributions and updated through natural-gradient variational inference. A novel dual-selection optimization strategy is introduced to jointly search for optimal candidate operators and network topology branches, achieving an explicit balance between model complexity and hardware latency. Furthermore, an in-search channel pruning strategy is incorporated to compress the search space and prevent the combinatorial growth of the channel configuration space. Comparative analysis and real-world welding experiments demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a high processing speed of 78 frames per second (FPS) on a legacy central processing unit (CPU)-above the 60 fps acquisition rate of the sensor-while maintaining a mean positioning error within 0.15 mm on the measurement plane. These results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves detection accuracy comparable to heavyweight detectors while offering an order-of-magnitude advantage in inference speed and model size, validating its suitability for low-cost industrial deployment.

title: MultiNet: Improving Gaze Estimation via Face-to-Camera Distance and Multi-Branch Learning.
authors: Nikita Ligostaev; Nicola Conci; Roberto Passerone; Andrey Somov
abstract: We present MultiNet, a multi-branch pipeline that directly predicts the gaze vector or the point of gaze from multiple modalities derived from a single camera capture. In particular, we address the under-explored use of metric face-to-camera distance estimated from a conventional RGB web camera for appearance-based gaze estimation, in contrast to many distance-aware alternatives which require depth sensors, stereo rigs, or additional hardware. The proposed method employs a convolutional neural network (CNN) with attentional feature fusion and integrates cropped face images, left and right eye patches, head-pose information, and estimated camera-to-face distance. We also introduce NLGaze, a 141,000-image dataset collected for unconstrained and natural desktop settings, thereby emphasizing real-world applicability. In a person-specific real-time evaluation, MultiNet-Base reaches a root mean square error (RMSE) of 43.01 pixels at 15 frames per second (FPS) on a desktop with an off-the-shelf web-camera. We evaluate the proposed method against representative state-of-the-art solutions on benchmark datasets. MultiNet achieves angular errors of 2.94°, 7.47°, and 7.58° at best on the MPIIFaceGaze, Gaze360, and NLGaze datasets, respectively, demonstrating competitive or superior performance in appearance-based gaze estimation. The results of the ablation study show that the attentional feature fusion mechanism and the addition of the estimated distance input to the set of input modalities result in significant angular error reduction.

authors: Sudheer Tale; Soibampahel M; Mrudula K; Ritisha B; Subodh K; Girish S
abstract: A 20 – year – old male without any previous comorbidity presented to pulmonary medicine outpatient department with complaints of dull aching chest pain on right side, dry cough and shortness of breath for the pastone year. He was non vegetarian and had no addictions. On general physical examination his vitals were stableand respiratory system examination revealed decreased breath sounds in the right hemithorax. All his routineblood investigations were normal. Chest radiograph revealed homogenous opacity in the right middle andlower zones. Contrast enhanced computed tomography of thorax and abdomen showed a well defined encapsulatedcystic lesion of size 12x10x14cm with internal floating membranes (water lily sign or Camelotte sign) with masseffect on adjacent lung parenchyma causing atelectasis and compression of adjacent vessels (Figure 1). Hydatid serology (IgG) was positive. Patient was treated symptomatically and referred for surgical intervention.

title: RELATION OF HEART WEIGHT WITH AGE AND WEIGHT OF CADAVER
authors: Jolly Agarwal; Virendra Kumar
abstract: Introduction: Height, weight, and age of person has significant impact on the normal size of heart. These parameters need to be considered when cut-off values indicating the need for treatment or even surgery are established. The aim of present work is to study the relation of weight of the heart with age and weight of cadaver. Material and Methods: The study was performed in the Department of Anatomy, Shri Ram Murti Smarak Institute of Medical Sciences, Bareilly on 30 hearts from embalmed cadavers. The hearts were procured from the cadavers available in our department. The heart was thoroughly cleaned and measurements were taken. Results: The mean heart weight was 223.37 ± 57.78 g. Significant relationship between age of the cadaver and weight of the heart (p=0.0004), weight of cadaver and weight of heart (p=0.0001) was observed. Conclusion: The above study provides valuable data of the heart in our geographical location, which may be useful for cardiac surgeons and physicians.

abstract: Abstract The theoretical paradigm for management of aortic stenosis (AS) assumes an early diagnosis, with surveillance until symptoms develop, followed by an elective intervention. In current practice, however, acute decompensation of aortic stenosis (ADAS) leading to hospital admission is commonplace, and one quarter of transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) procedures performed in the UK are now performed urgently on patients with ADAS. Acute decompensation and hospital admission often reflects a failure of the upstream AS pathway, typically encompassing late diagnosis, delays to work-up, and challenges with delivery of definitive procedural intervention. Patients presenting with ADAS have a higher prevalence of cardiac damage, frailty, and comorbidities, all of which impact long-term outcome. This Viewpoint reviews the current paradigm and its limitations, before considering strategies to reduce the frequency of ADAS, and outlining clinical and research priorities to better understand ADAS, to provide better standardisation of care pathways in ADAS, and to improve outcomes for patients that present with ADAS.

title: Suspected atrioesophageal fistula complicated by coronary air embolism after catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation: direct angiographic visualization and catheter aspiration in a case report
authors: Chao Yang; Xiaobin Zeng; Shihai Wang; Chaoju Wang; Jianjun Lan; Yahong Wen; Zaiyong Zheng
abstract: Atrioesophageal fistula is a rare but fatal complication of catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation(AF). It may present with infection, dysphagia or other swallowing-related symptoms, neurologic events, and systemic air embolism; coronary air embolism is even less common. Case summary An 84-year-old woman was admitted with recurrent palpitations lasting 1 h, approximately 1 month after radiofrequency catheter ablation for atrial fibrillation and left atrial appendage closure(RFCA & LAAC). On admission, she was in sinus rhythm and had a normal cardiac troponin level. Four hours after admission, she abruptly became unresponsive and developed fever and severe respiratory abnormalities. Electrocardiography subsequently showed ST-segment elevation in leads II, III, and aVF. Emergency coronary angiography demonstrated gas in the mid right coronary artery with TIMI 0 distal flow, and catheter aspiration was performed. Computed tomography (CT) of the head and chest revealed gas at multiple sites, including the intracranial compartment, cardiac chambers, and great vessels. Blood cultures grew Streptococcus constellatus and other streptococci. Given the recent left atrial ablation, acute neurologic and myocardial ischemic manifestations, multisite intravascular gas, and bacteremia with organisms associated with the oropharyngeal or gastrointestinal flora, an atrioesophageal fistula complicated by systemic air embolism was strongly suspected. Her condition deteriorated rapidly, and she developed cardiac arrest and died approximately 27 h after admission. Conclusion Atrioesophageal fistula and coronary air embolism should be considered in patients who develop fever, impaired consciousness, or acute ST-segment elevation within several weeks of atrial fibrillation ablation. Coronary angiography can directly visualize intracoronary gas and allow catheter aspiration; however, the certainty of an atrioesophageal fistula diagnosis should remain commensurate with the available imaging evidence.

title: Mosaic RASopathies: comprehensive genetic and clinicopathological analysis for diagnosis and management
authors: Tatiana Belysheva; Tatiana V. Nasedkina; Екатерина Евгеньевна Зеленова; Vera V. Semenova; Natalia Semenova; G. B. Sagoyan; Irina S. Kletskaya; Yana V. Vishnevskaya; Елена Вячеславовна Шарапова; Kristina Kulikova; Pavel Vlasov; Alexandra Botkina; Margarita Belogurova; Marina Yu. Dorofeeva; Тимур Валиев; Светлана Рафаэлевна Варфоломеева
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract: Introduction Mosaic RASopathies are rare conditions caused by postzygotic mutations arising during embryonic development in genes of the RAS/MAPK signaling pathway. They are mainly characterized by a combination of epidermal nevi and extracutaneous manifestations. Distinguishing between different entities can be challenging because of their substantial clinical and genetic overlap. Our aim was to demonstrate the importance of genetic background for accurate diagnosis and further prognostic assessment of disease progression by analyzing genotype–phenotype correlations within this clinical group. Methods The study enrolled 18 patients (10 male and 8 female patients) ranging in age from 1 month to 21 years with congenital craniofacial nevi and variable extracutaneous abnormalities. DNA isolated from peripheral blood leukocytes and affected tissues (nevus and tumor) was analyzed using a targeted next-generation sequencing (NGS) panel covering RAS/MAPK pathway genes, followed by Sanger sequencing. Results Eight patients were diagnosed with Schimmelpenning–Feuerstein–Mims syndrome caused by postzygotic pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in the HRAS (n = 4) or KRAS (n = 4) genes. Seven patients were clinically diagnosed with phacomatosis pigmentokeratotica (PPK), and mosaic genetic variants were identified in the HRAS (n = 4), KRAS (n = 2), or BRAF (n = 1) genes. In two additional patients with similar phenotypes, somatic mutations in PIK3CA (n = 1) and FGFR2 (n = 1) were identified in affected skin, while in one further case, no clinically significant variant was detected. Discussion We compared the spectrum of extracutaneous anomalies according to the affected gene by combining our data with data from other clinical cases of mosaic RASopathies described in the literature. In summary, 53 cases with HRAS postzygotic variants and 41 cases with KRAS variants were included in the analysis of genotype–phenotype correlations. Hypophosphatemic rickets (HR) and malignant tumors were associated with pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in the HRAS gene, while ophthalmological, neurological, cardiovascular, and renal disorders were more common in KRAS -mutant patients. Conclusion Thus, genetic testing of affected tissue in comparison to normal tissue (peripheral blood) is essential for accurate diagnosis of these mosaic disorders. Consideration of clinical manifestations and the identified genotype–phenotype correlations may further assist in determining prognosis and guiding patient management.

title: Coronary artery compression in percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation: a case series
authors: Rujira Buntharikpornpun; Supaporn Roymanee; Worakan Promphan; Phuoc Duong
abstract: Catastrophic complications of coronary artery compression after percutaneous pulmonary valve implantation (PPVI) are uncommon in patients with a dysfunctional native right ventricular outflow tract after Tetralogy of Fallot repair (rTOF). Nonetheless, we report three rTOFs with a high risk of compromising coronary blood flow for PPVI. This risk has been elucidated by multimodal assessments, including robust pre-procedural cardiac computed tomography and meticulous balloon interrogation with selective coronary angiography.

title: Evaluation of ChatGPT for Myocardial Infarction Health Information: Expert Accuracy Assessment and User Trust Survey
authors: Eman Elsheikh; Abdullah Ahmed Aladsani; Yousef Abdullatif Aljohar; Ghala Abdulaziz Alzahrani; Ali Mohammed Nasser Alsadah; Maryam Ahmed Almuhaysh; Walah Sami Rashid alowaynan; Rehab H. Werida
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: Artificial intelligence chatbots, particularly ChatGPT, have emerged as increasingly popular sources of health information for the general public. However, concerns persist regarding the accuracy, safety, and appropriateness of AI-generated medical advice, especially for life-threatening conditions such as myocardial infarction. Objectives: This study aimed to evaluate the accuracy, completeness, and safety of ChatGPT-generated responses and information to public questions about heart attacks, assess user perceptions and trust, and compare AI-generated content with expert-validated sources. Methods: A cross-sectional study was conducted between January and March 2026. A total of 73 commonly asked heart attack-related questions were submitted to ChatGPT (GPT-4), and responses were independently evaluated by two expert reviewers and one external reviewer using standardized rubric assessing accuracy, completeness, clarity, safety, and tone. Inter-rater reliability was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients. In parallel, a survey of 352 participants evaluated user perceptions, trust, and behavioral use of ChatGPT for medical information. Statistical analyses included descriptive statistics, group comparisons, correlation analyses, and multivariable regression models to identify predictors of trust and satisfaction. Results: Expert reviewers assigned high ratings for accuracy (mean: 4.62 ± 0.62 and 4.48 ± 0.63) and safety (mean: 4.78 ± 0.51 and 4.05 ± 0.50), with substantial inter-rater agreement (ICC = 0.788). In contrast, the external reviewer documented considerably lower completeness ratings (2.59 ± 0.57), revealing deficiencies in information coverage. Remarkably, 40.6% of respondents indicated they had followed ChatGPT's medical recommendations without seeking professional consultation, while 17.6% reported depending on the chatbot during urgent medical situations. Levels of user trust and satisfaction were moderate, showing significant correlations with perceived accuracy, usage frequency, and healthcare-related educational background. Conclusions: Expert assessments confirmed that ChatGPT generally provides accurate and safe cardiovascular health information; nevertheless, considerable inter-reviewer variability—especially the markedly lower completeness scores from the external evaluator—reveals significant gaps in content depth. These results indicate that ChatGPT functions more appropriately as an adjunctive educational resource rather than a replacement for professional medical consultation, emphasizing the necessity for enhanced safety mechanisms, clearer user instructions, and standardized content protocols when addressing high-stakes health topics. ChatGPT should be considered an adjunctive resource rather than a substitute for urgent professional medical assessment in suspected heart attack cases.

title: Parenteral Nutrition as a Strategic Therapeutic Option for Onco-Geriatric Rehabilitation After Total Gastrectomy and Anastomotic Stenosis Complicated by an Aorto-Esophageal Fistula: A Case Report
authors: Houssam Eddine Belaid; João Gabriel De Carvalho; Mariangela Gagliano
journal: Reports — Medical Cases Images and Videos
abstract: Background and Clinical Significance: The nutritional management of onco-geriatric patients after a total gastrectomy remains a challenge, especially in the context of postoperative complications, such as stenosis of the esophagojejunal anastomosis, and in the presence of an aorto-esophageal fistula. Parenteral nutrition is a relevant therapeutic option to maintain nutritional support and enable rehabilitation when oral and enteral feeding are no longer feasible in this specific clinical context; Case Presentation: We report here the case of a 76-year-old patient who underwent a total gastrectomy for gastric adenocarcinoma with several dilated and stented esophagojejunal anastomoses. During the first postoperative year, the nutritional adaptation facilitated rehabilitation and helped him recover well. However, the occurrence of an aorto-esophageal fistula and its treatment with thoracic endovascular aortic repair (TEVAR) made oral and enteral feeding impossible. This was associated with persistent asthenia, physical deconditioning, sarcopenia, weight loss, exercise intolerance, and increased dependence for activities of daily living. Although parenteral nutrition allowed for nutritional stability and the beginning of rehabilitation, a suspected nosocomial infection involving the aortic endograft led to his death before his treatment was complete; Conclusions: This case highlights the relevance of parenteral nutrition as a therapeutic option to continue rehabilitation when enteral access is judged unacceptably risky. However, the risk of infectious complications in the context of malnutrition can compromise the prognosis, and any suspicion of infection involving prosthetic material should be documented microbiologically as completely as possible whenever compatible with the patient’s care objectives. Onco-geriatric assessment to manage older patients with esophagogastric cancer is recommended.

title: Takayasu arteritis in the context of polyautoimmunity: clinical clustering, shared immunopathogenesis, and cardiovascular phenotypes
authors: Muneeb Saifullah; Urooj Fatima; Muhammad Ashhad Usman; Musfirah Riaz; Ghazi Rizvi; Muhammad Alyan Khan; Zainab Attiq; Aleena Saleemi; Yumna Tariq; Zainab Ayub; Amna Sabir; Arfa Madni; Ayman Noor; Saleena Ali; Ikra Rana
abstract: Abstract Background Takayasu arteritis is a rare, chronic large-vessel vasculitis that primarily affects young women, particularly the aorta and its branches. It is traditionally regarded as an isolated vascular disease, and its coexistence with other systemic autoimmune diseases is uncommon, having been described mainly in case reports and small series. These reports, together with shared genetic and immunological features, have nevertheless prompted interest in whether TAK can be considered within the concept of polyautoimmunity. Objective This narrative review explores the relationship between Takayasu arteritis and polyautoimmunity, highlighting current evidence on shared immune mechanisms, disease clustering, and cardiovascular manifestations, and considers whether these findings support an autoimmune spectrum. Methods A comprehensive literature search was conducted in PubMed, Google Scholar, and the Cochrane Library for studies published since 2002. MeSH terms and keywords related to Takayasu arteritis (TAK), polyautoimmunity, and cardiovascular manifestations were used. Evidence from international registries, meta-analyses, and retrospective cohorts was reviewed. Studies were selected based on relevance to shared immunopathogenic mechanisms, the 2022 ACR/EULAR classification criteria, and Numano angiographic types. The literature was synthesized to evaluate the impact of coexisting autoimmune diseases on cardiovascular outcomes and treatment response in TAK. Results Takayasu arteritis (TAK) has been reported to coexist with other autoimmune diseases, particularly spondyloarthritis-spectrum disorders, and, less frequently and largely in case reports, systemic lupus erythematosus, rheumatoid arthritis, Behçet disease, and inflammatory bowel disease. These reported associations are supported by shared genetic susceptibility, especially HLA-B52, and common immune pathways involving the Th1/Th17 axis, IL-6, and TNF-α. Persistent activation of these pathways contributes to chronic systemic inflammation, which may worsen vascular damage and promote cardiovascular complications such as aortic regurgitation, renovascular hypertension, coronary ostial stenosis, and cerebrovascular ischemic events. Limited observational data suggest that coexisting autoimmune disease may be linked to a more treatment-resistant course, with a higher need for biologic agents such as tocilizumab or TNF inhibitors. Conclusion Although coexistence with other autoimmune diseases is uncommon and the supporting evidence is limited, considering Takayasu arteritis (TAK) within the spectrum of polyautoimmunity may help clinicians recognize shared immune mechanisms. Evaluation for coexisting autoimmune conditions at diagnosis and during follow-up, guided by clinical suspicion, may facilitate earlier recognition, guide individualized immunomodulatory treatment, and, where appropriate, enable a single therapeutic agent to address overlapping diseases. A multidisciplinary approach may further improve long-term outcomes by reducing the risk of severe cardiovascular and other end-organ complications.

title: A data-driven framework to identify restenosis-prone regions in femoral arteries from geometric and inflow waveform parameters
authors: Chotirawee Chatpattanasiri; Federica Ninno; Vanessa Díaz‐Zuccarini; Stavroula Balabani
journal: Journal of The Royal Society Interface
abstract: Haemodynamic indices derived from computational fluid dynamics (CFD), such as time-averaged wall shear stress (TAWSS) and oscillatory shear index (OSI), are closely associated with restenosis risk in peripheral arterial disease (PAD). We present a machine learning-reduced order modelling (ML-ROM) framework to predict critical, restenosis-prone, haemodynamic regions accounting for both vessel geometries and inlet flow waveforms. We generated 500 parameterized virtual femoral-artery geometries, each paired with a synthetic physiologically realistic inflow waveform. CFD was used to obtain the wall shear stress (WSS) distribution, from which TAWSS and OSI were computed. Critical regions were then defined by applying different thresholding criteria based on TAWSS and OSI, as found in the literature. These were then used to construct ROMs using Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD), and to train ML models from which the critical regions could be reconstructed. Four ML architectures were explored: a geometric-parameter-only model and three alternatives that also incorporate inflow waveform information via Fourier coefficients, long short-term memory (LSTM), and convolutional neural networks (CNN). The Fourier models achieved the highest predictive performance, with the median values of balanced accuracy (BA) exceeding 0.92 across all critical-region definitions. The model also offered a substantial speed-up ratio of the order of 109 compared with traditional CFD.

title: Multidimensional Echocardiographic Parameters Predict Left Ventricular Functional Recovery After Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting
authors: Man Zhang; Jun Xia; Xiaoling Wan; Xuejiao Chen
abstract: AIM: This study aimed to investigate the predictive value of preoperative and early postoperative echocardiographic parameters for left ventricular function recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), and to evaluate the relationship between functional recovery and 1-year clinical prognosis.METHODS: This retrospective cohort included 214 patients undergoing first-time elective CABG at The First Affiliated Hospital of Yangtze University between January 2022 and October 2024. Transthoracic echocardiography was performed preoperatively, 3–7 days postoperatively, and at 6 months to evaluate left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), global longitudinal strain (GLS), left atrial volume index (LAVI), and ratio of early mitral inflow velocity to early diastolic mitral annular velocity (E/e′). Based on 6‑month LVEF change, patients were divided into recovery (ΔLVEF ≥5%) and non‑recovery (ΔLVEF <5%) groups. Multivariate logistic regression was used to identify independent predictors, and the corresponding models were established and validated. Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) were recorded at 1‑year follow‑up.RESULTS: Of the 214 patients enrolled in the study, functional recovery of the left ventricle was observed in 128 individuals, corresponding to 59.8% of the cohort. Multivariate analysis identified several preoperative and procedural variables as independent predictors of functional recovery, including left atrial volume index (LAVI), left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD), left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD), left atrial diameter (LAD), Synergy between Percutaneous Coronary Intervention with TAXUS and Cardiac Surgery (SYNTAX) score, and the number of graft vessels. Age, preoperative LVEF, and e′ velocity were independently associated with lower odds of functional recovery. Global longitudinal strain (GLS) and diabetes history showed no independent predictive value. The clinical-echocardiographic combined model demonstrated excellent discrimination and showed higher discriminative performance than the basic clinical model and conventional echocardiographic model. Subgroup analysis revealed that GLS showed no independent predictive value across all LVEF subgroups (p > 0.05), whereas LAVI and LAD were significant predictors in patients with LVEF ≥40% (including the 40%–49% subgroup), but showed no predictive relevance in those with LVEF <40%. Early postoperative ΔLVEF predicted 6-month functional recovery with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.846. After one year of follow‑up, the recovery group exhibited a markedly lower rate of MACE than the non‑recovery group, with left ventricular functional recovery serving as an independent protective factor against MACE.CONCLUSIONS: Preoperative structural parameters, including LAVI, LVEDD, LVESD, and LAD, are independent imaging biomarkers for predicting left ventricular functional recovery after CABG. GLS and E/e′ ratio show no independent predictive value in this study. The integrated model combining clinical factors with multi-dimensional echocardiographic parameters demonstrates excellent discriminative ability. Early postoperative LVEF improvement strongly predicts 6-month functional recovery, while postoperative recovery of left ventricular function is associated with a significantly lower 1-year MACE risk.

title: External validation of the D-PACE score for predicting late high-grade atrioventricular block after transcatheter aortic valve replacement in a Colombian cohort
authors: Juan David Zuluaga-Monroy; Hugo Oswaldo Alvarado Mora; Diana Fernanda Bohorquez Gonzalez; J.J. Sierra; Edgar Fernando Hurtado Ordoñez
abstract: Background Transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) carries a clinically significant risk of late high-grade atrioventricular block (AVB), yet no validated tool exists to predict this complication in Latin-American populations. The D-PACE score was developed in European cohorts for this purpose. Methods In a retrospective cohort of 175 consecutive TAVR procedures at a Colombian center (2012–2025), 141 patients met inclusion criteria for D-PACE validation. The primary outcome was late high-grade AVB (≥Mobitz type II) occurring between 24 h and 30 days post-TAVR. Discrimination, logistic-regression calibration, and decision curve analysis were performed. Results Late AVB occurred in 31 patients (22.0%), with 80.6% of events within 72 h. The D-PACE score demonstrated good discrimination (AUC 0.82; 95% CI 0.71–0.92; sensitivity 77.4%, specificity 86.4% at a cutoff of 5.5 points; NPV 93.1%). Late AVB rates rose progressively across strata: 5.9% (low-risk, score 0–3), 8.8% (intermediate, 4–5), and 61.5% (high-risk, ≥6), with the high-risk group concentrating 77.4% of all events. Decision curve analysis confirmed net clinical benefit across threshold probabilities from 8% to 60%. All four low-risk events occurred among valve-in-valve patients assigned a score of 0 per the original algorithm; excluding this subgroup ( N = 114), the AUC rose to 0.91 (95% CI 0.85–0.96) with zero low-risk events. In an exploratory analysis applying the full seven-variable scoring uniformly, including valve-in-valve cases, the AUC was 0.90 (95% CI 0.85–0.95; NPV 96.7%), and 0.91 (95% CI 0.78–1.00) within the valve-in-valve subgroup ( N = 27, 4 events). Conclusions Applied as originally specified, the D-PACE score showed good discrimination for late high-grade AVB in this cohort (AUC 0.82; 95% CI 0.71–0.92). The algorithm's automatic low-risk classification of valve-in-valve patients was not supported (14.8% AVB rate). Discrimination was higher both in the sensitivity analysis excluding valve-in-valve cases and in the exploratory analysis applying the seven-variable scoring uniformly, indicating that the scoring variables transfer well while the valve-in-valve exemption warrants reconsideration. These findings provide the first external validation of D-PACE in Latin America.

title: Implementation of IRRAflow active irrigation in neurosurgical patients: A case series and literature overview
authors: Matteo Palermoit; Domenico Policicchio; Domenico La Torre; Marina Romozzi; Carmelo Lucio Sturiale; Francesco Signorelli
abstract: BACKGROUND: Active fluid management systems such as IRRAflow aim to overcome the limitations of passive external drains by enabling simultaneous automated irrigation and aspiration in a closed circuit. In acute and chronic subdural hematoma (a/cSDH), it enables active subdural irrigation, whereas in subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH), intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and ventriculitis, it allows continuous ventricular CSF exchange and, when indicated, intrathecal administration of therapeutic agents. METHODS: A literature analysis identified studies reporting IRRAflow use for SAH, SDH, IVH, or ventriculitis. Additionally, a single-center retrospective series of 13 consecutive patients treated with IRRAflow was analyzed, focusing on clinical course, complications, and outcomes. RESULTS: Thirty studies comprising 345 patients were included in the literature analysis. In cSDH, clinical resolution was reported in 40 cases (90.9%), with recurrence in 3 patients (6.8%) and no reported infections or catheter obstructions. In aSDH, only 1/11 patient experienced clinical deterioration and required conversion to craniotomy. In IVH, outcomes were more variable, with complete resolution in 14/36 cases (38.9%), clinical improvement in 15/36 (41.7%), deterioration in 1/36 (2.8%), and death in 6 (16.7%). In ventriculitis, largely reported in case reports and small case series, resolution or improvement was achieved in 27/35 patients (77.1%), while mortality was 8/35 (22.9%). In aSAH, 7/23 (30.4%) patients died from complications of the hemorrhage. Vasospasm occurred in 7/23 (30.4%) patients, including two who subsequently died, while 2/23 (8.7%) required permanent shunting; both were survivors who had experienced vasospasm. No device-related complications were reported. Our institutional cohort included 6 patients with IVH, 4 with cSDH, and 3 with ventriculitis. Among the IVH cases, 3/6 patients died before discharge, 1 died during follow-up, whereas the other 2 had an mRS score of 3 and 2 at last follow-up. Among patients with cSDH, 3/4 achieved favorable functional recovery at follow-up, while 1/4 died before discharge because of complications unrelated to IRRAflow. Among the 3 patients with ventriculitis, 1 died following a complication related to urokinase infusion after adjunctive urokinase administration, whereas the remaining 2 (66.7%) achieved resolution or improvement. CONCLUSIONS: Both the institutional cohort and the literature search showed promising results for the use of IRRAflow in cSDH. Results on ventriculitis, aSAH and aSDH are still uncertain due to the small sample sizes. Regarding IVH, neither the exploratory review nor our institutional case series identified a clear clinical benefit associated with IRRAflow use. Nevertheless, the available evidence remains limited by predominantly observational, small and heterogeneous studies, precluding comparative conclusions.

title: Machine learning–based prediction of in-hospital postoperative ischemic stroke following off-pump coronary artery bypass grafting
authors: Zhengdong Kong; Wen-Long Zou; Guang-Pu Fan; Wenqing Zhang; Chun Liu; Hui Xue; Chaobin Wang; Lu-Feng Zhang; Dan Miao; Xiaoqing Li; Bin Cai; Rui-Yuan Guan; Xiu-Bin Yang; Qing-Hua Cui; Guang-Zhi Liu

title: Microvascular resistance reserve: insights into discordant resting and hyperemic epicardial coronary physiology
authors: Aswin Babu; Isobelle Goldrick; Billy Broadbent; Rania Faeq; Charley Ann Budgeon; Roopa Krishnamoorthy; Primero Ng; Cara Barnes; D. Sankhesara; Avadhesh Saraswat; I. Shiekh; James Marangou; Richard F. Alcock; Rachel C. Orme; Carl Johann Schultz; Graham S. Hillis; J. Spiro
abstract: Introduction Discordance between resting and hyperemic epicardial physiology is commonbut mechanistically unclear. Microvascular resistance reserve (MRR), a novelindex of vasodilatory capacity, may provide insight. We aimed to characterizethe prevalence and microvascular substrate of FFR/RFR discordance, andwhether MRR is independently associated with discordant phenotypes. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 891 vessels from 723 consecutive patients with paired resting full-cycle ratio (RFR) and fractional flow reserve (FFR) measurements (June 2018–October 2024). Vessels were categorized as concordant or discordant. An operator-selected subset of 210 underwent coronary flow reserve (CFR), index of microvascular resistance (IMR), and MRR assessment. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of each discordant phenotype (FFR−/RFR+ and FFR+/RFR−). Results Discordance was present in 195 vessels (22%); 121 (13.6%) FFR−/RFR+ and 74 (8.3%) FFR+/RFR−. Discordance was more common in the LAD (25% vs. 17%, OR 1.68, 95% CI 1.20–2.36, p = 0.003), driven predominantly by the FFR−/RFR+ phenotype (OR 2.43, 95% CI 1.56–3.78, p < 0.001). In the microvascular subset ( n = 210), reduced CFR (OR 0.77, 95% CI 0.59–0.97, p = 0.039) and reduced MRR (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.65–0.97, p = 0.037) were independently associated with the FFR−/RFR+ phenotype, while neither predicted the FFR+/RFR− phenotype. However, among 45 discordant vessels with microvascular data, MRR provided greater discrimination than CFR (AUC 0.712, 95% CI 0.539–0.884 vs. 0.608, 95% CI 0.434–0.783, p = 0.018). Discussion These exploratory, hypothesis-generating findings suggest that impaired microvascular vasodilatory reserve, expressed predominantly as elevated resting flow, may contribute mechanistically to the FFR−/RFR+ phenotype.

title: Vasospastic Angina and Cardiac Arrest
authors: Kazuya Tateishi; Yuichi Saito; Ken Kato; Hideki Kitahara; Yoshio Kobayashi
abstract: Vasospastic angina (VSA) is an important and potentially treatable cause of cardiac arrest (CA) and may account for approximately 2–10% of otherwise unexplained cases of out-of-hospital CA. VSA can sometimes be diagnosed by spontaneous coronary spasm during emergency coronary angiography or by transient ST-segment elevation during a spontaneous attack after resuscitation. However, because coronary spasm is transient and may not be evident during the initial evaluation, provocation testing after clinical stabilization may be required to establish the diagnosis in otherwise unexplained cases. Once VSA is diagnosed, vasodilator therapy, particularly calcium-channel blockers, is the mainstay of treatment. Nevertheless, survivors of VSA-related CA may remain at risk of recurrent lethal ventricular arrhythmias despite medical therapy. Evaluation for alternative or overlapping arrhythmogenic disorders, including cardiomyopathies and channelopathies, should therefore be considered even after a diagnosis of VSA, and implantable cardioverter-defibrillator implantation may be considered in selected patients according to the risk of recurrence and response to medical therapy. Further prospective studies, including randomized controlled trials, are needed to determine whether systematic provocation testing followed by targeted therapy reduces recurrent ventricular arrhythmias and CA and improves long-term outcomes.

title: A novel LARP7 variant expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome and reveals transcriptomic dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways
authors: Mozan Hassan; Manal Irshaid; Aalia Batool; Wadima Ali; Latifa Ba Qehaizel; Shamma Alzaabi; Shamma AlNuaimi; Sara Saeed; Fatma Al Jasmi; Nadia A. Akawi
journal: Frontiers in Cell and Developmental Biology
abstract: Background LARP7 encodes a critical scaffold protein of the 7SK small nuclear ribonucleoprotein (7SK snRNP) complex that regulates RNA polymerase II transcriptional elongation. Biallelic loss-of-function variants in LARP7 cause Alazami syndrome, a rare neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by intellectual disability, growth restriction, and distinctive craniofacial features. However, the transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency in human cells remain poorly understood, and the phenotypic spectrum of the disorder is incompletely defined. Methods We investigated a 6-year-old boy with clinically diagnosed Alazami syndrome who carried a novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant. Clinical evaluation and exome sequencing of blood-derived genomic DNA were performed, while quantitative PCR, Western blotting, and transcriptomic analysis were conducted using patient-derived dermal fibroblasts. Transcriptomic consequences of LARP7 deficiency were assessed by RNA sequencing, followed by single-subject differential expression, pathway enrichment, and network analyses. Results The patient presented with classical features of Alazami syndrome and tetralogy of Fallot, a cardiac manifestation not previously reported in the disorder. The novel homozygous LARP7 frameshift variant resulted in marked depletion of LARP7 transcripts and complete loss of full-length protein. Transcriptome-wide analysis identified 1,224 dysregulated genes involved in extracellular matrix organization, developmental remodeling, cell-cycle regulation, and immune signaling. Pathway and network analyses highlighted dysregulation of STAT3-associated signaling together with SMAD3-linked extracellular matrix and developmental programs, identifying candidate developmental and tissue-remodeling pathways that warrant further investigation in disease-relevant models. Conclusion This study provides the first comprehensive transcriptomic characterization of genetically confirmed LARP7 deficiency in primary human cells and potentially expands the phenotypic spectrum of Alazami syndrome. The findings reveal widespread dysregulation of developmental and extracellular matrix pathways, offering new insight into the molecular basis of the multisystem manifestations of Alazami syndrome and providing a framework for future functional and genotype–phenotype studies.

title: Parental attitudes toward the vaccination of children diagnosed with congenital heart disease: a cross-sectional comparative study
authors: Ruken Yıldız Cengiz; Alper Akın; Mehmet Türe; Duygu Uç; Vasfiye Demir Pervane; Asuman Akar; Pakize Gamze Erten Bucaktepe
abstract: The presence of chronic disease in children is an important factor affecting vaccination status. The aim of this study was to evaluate the attitudes toward childhood vaccinations of parents of children diagnosed with congenital heart disease (CHD) on presentation at the Pediatric Cardiology Outpatient Clinic of Dicle University Hospital and the vaccination status of the children through comparisons with the parents of healthy children. This cross-sectional comparative study included a case group of parents of children who were diagnosed with CHD who presented at the Pediatric Cardiology Outpatient Clinic of Dicle University Hospital between 01.06.2022 and 01.06.2023. The control group consisted of parents of children who had not been diagnosed with CHD. The Parent Attitudes about Childhood Vaccines (PACV) scale and a questionnaire regarding the participants’ sociodemographic characteristics and the vaccination status of the children were used to collect data. A total of 731 parents were evaluated, 274 in the case group and 457 in the control group. No significant difference between the groups with respect to the rates of application of the vaccinations included in the Turkish National Vaccination Schedule (NVS) was detected ( p > 0.05 for all the variables). The rates of rotavirus and meningococcus vaccinations were determined to be significantly greater in the control group ( p < 0.001, p < 0.001). In the comparisons between the case and control groups, vaccine hesitancy was significantly greater in the control group ( p = 0.006). The total raw PACV score, the converted PACV score, and the general attitude subdomain score were significantly greater in the control group ( p < 0.001, p < 0.001, p = 0.019, respectively). In the case group, the rate of vaccine hesitancy among the parents of children with cyanotic heart disease was greater ( p = 0.038). The results of this study revealed that the rate of vaccine hesitancy was lower for parents of children diagnosed with CHD than for parents of healthy children. However, cyanotic heart disease was associated with a significantly higher rate of vaccine hesitancy. Vaccine hesitancy was also associated with several sociodemographic characteristics, vaccine-related knowledge and economic factors.

title: Blood pressure improvement and long-term outcomes after carotid stenting in patients with hypertension and atherosclerotic carotid stenosis
authors: Haodi Zhang; Hufei Chang; feng jiang; yi jia; jiaxin wang; Ze Cheng; Yuhao Lin; zhaosheng jia; Jiale Wang; Yichu Guo; llong cong; Jiafeng Han; lin yang

title: Early and Long-Term Results of 101 Consecutive Patients After Transcarotid Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation
authors: Damian Hudziak; Monika Gruz-Kwapisz; Radosław Parma; Wojciech Wańha; Sylwia Gładysz-Wańha; Wojciech Wojakowski; Radosław Gocoł
abstract: Background/Objectives: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation through the common carotid artery (TC-TAVI) is one of the possible treatment options for patients with ineligible transfemoral approach. The aim of our study was to evaluate the efficacy and safety of patients treated with TC-TAVI in early and long-term follow-up. Methods: The study included patients with severe aortic stenosis treated with TC-TAVI. In-hospital outcomes, early, long-term follow-up were presented in accordance with the VARC-3 recommendations. Results: The analysis presented 101 patients. We observed high procedural success-97% (n = 98). The number of VARC-3 incidents: 3.96% major vascular complications; 0.99% myocardial infarction; 0.99% cardiac tamponade; 0.99% life-threatening bleeding; 3.96% cerebrovascular incidents. The NYHA class decreased significantly compared to the pre-procedure value (2 [1–2] vs. 3 [3–3]; p < 0.001). There was a significant improvement in postprocedural cerebral oximetry values compared to baseline on both the implanted and contralateral sides (67.5 [63–71]% vs. 70 [63.5–75]%; p < 0.05) and (67 [64–71]% vs. 71 [64–76]%; p < 0.05), respectively. The 30-day, 1-year, and 2-year survival rates were 94.1%, 80.2%, and 69.3%, respectively. In the univariate analysis, BAV (HR 4.54; 95% CI: 1.14–17.99; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 7.32; 95% CI: 2.59–20.65; p < 0.001) were significantly associated with two-year mortality. In an exploratory adjusted Cox regression analysis, BAV (HR 2.63; 95% CI: 1.07–6.45; p = 0.03) and LVEF ≤ 35% (HR 3.48; 95% CI: 1.67–7.24; p < 0.001) were associated with higher 2-year mortality. Conclusions: Our single-center, observational report indicated feasibility and good observed outcomes of the TC-TAVI procedure in an experienced clinical team.

title: The durability of different anchoring points and anchoring types in the left ventricle in an ex vivo porcine model
authors: Henrik Bjursten; Per N Wierup; Sasha M. Koul; Matthias Götberg; Magnus Dencker
abstract: Abstract Objective Surgical mitral valve repair, including anchoring in different parts of the mitral apparatus, is the standard of care for severe mitral regurgitation. Various percutaneous approaches have been developed and are currently under development, but are struggling with durable results. This study investigates the durability of different anatomic anchoring points and anchoring types in the left ventricle. Material and Methods Anchoring was tested with PTFE sutures or a 5 mm helix at three locations: the head of the papillary muscle, the lateral wall of the ventricle, and the apex of the ventricle. An accelerated life test was performed with 300 cycles at 3 N for each anchoring. Durability was assessed by measuring compliance (strain in mm until 3 N is reached), migration (change in strain from the first to the last cycle), and the occurrence of dehiscence. Results The lowest numerical strain/compliance in the first cycle was observed at the head of the papillary muscle anchoring (both surgical and helix). Migration of strain limits over 300 cycles was seen for all locations. The lowest migration was numerically for helix in the papillary muscle. Conclusion PTFE in the head of the papillary muscle is standard practice in mitral valve repair and was used as a reference in the present study. The anchoring that yielded the most similar results was a helix in the papillary muscle, whereas other anchoring points showed greater compliance and/or migration.

title: Myocardial scar burden independently predicts response to cardiac resynchronization therapy
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Objectives: Cardiac resynchronization therapy (CRT) has been shown to improve quality of life and reduce mortality in patients with heart failure.Around 30 -45% are non-responders to CRT.Determinants of response to CRT have been extensively studied.Faithful efforts were exerted to improve selection criteria for CRT beyond standard measures of electrical dyssynchrony.We aimed to assess the predictive value of amount and distribution of myocardial fibrosis to identify responders to CRT compared to conventional measures.Methodology: 58 patients who underwent CRT implantation on the basis of standard indication were studied.All patients had available myocardial imaging (cardiac MRI or nuclear scan) prior to CRT.Images were analyzed for scar quantification and distribution.Multiple variables were studied.Receiver operator characteristic (ROC) curve analysis was used to evaluate the ability of Global scar to predict response to CRT.Results: 30 patients of 58 were non-responders to CRT. 27 patients had non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, while 31 patients had ischemic cardiomyopathy.19 patients (70.3%) in the non-ischemic group, and 9 patients (32.2%) in the ischemic group were responders to CRT, with a statistically significant difference, p-value: 0.002.A cutoff threshold of myocardial scar at 22.9% independently predicted response to CRT with a sensitivity of 70% and a specificity of 92.9%.Conclusion: Global myocardial scar burden predicted response to CRT independent of etiology, regional distribution, and measures of electrical dyssynchrony.

title: Transjugular implantation of a leadless pacemaker in a 97-year-old patient with severe kyphosis and tortuous femoral veins: a case report
authors: Minghuan Fu; Xue-Fei Tao; Jie Gao; Yong Shi; Biao Cheng; Wei Zhang; Xiao-Han Chen
abstract: Background Leadless pacemaker systems offer significant benefits for frail older adults by avoiding pocket- and lead-related complications. However, anatomical challenges including severe spinal deformities and significant venous tortuosity can complicate conventional transfemoral or trans-subclavian implantation. Case report A 97-year-old man with severe kyphosis, tortuous femoral veins, and high-grade atrioventricular block was referred for permanent pacing. Supine positioning for subclavian access was not feasible, and the femoral anatomy posed an unacceptably high procedural risk. Following a multidisciplinary assessment and procedural planning, a transjugular approach was selected. Implantation was performed with the patient in the left lateral decubitus position, using adapted fluoroscopic projections and temporary femoral pacing as backup. An Aveir ventricular response leadless pacemaker was successfully delivered via the right internal jugular vein. Final device parameters were satisfactory, with a sensing amplitude of 8.5 mV, a pacing threshold of 0.5 V at 0.4 ms, and an impedance of 510 Ω. No perioperative complications occurred. At follow-up, exertional dyspnea had resolved, and device performance remained stable. Conclusion This case demonstrates that transjugular implantation of a leadless pacemaker can be a safe and feasible alternative for older adults with complex anatomical limitations that contraindicate standard pacing approaches. Careful preprocedural assessment and adaptation of intraoperative techniques are essential for procedural success in high-risk settings.

title: Residual Mitral Regurgitation After Surgical Mitral Valve Repair and Long-Term Recurrence and Reintervention
authors: JM Kong; Mingyang Yu; Jingxin Zhou
abstract: Surgical mitral valve repair is the preferred treatment for degenerative mitral regurgitation (MR) and is also widely performed for MR of other etiologies; however, recurrent MR after repair is not uncommon and is associated with adverse left ventricular remodeling and increased risks of mitral valve reintervention and death. At the completion of repair, a small amount of residual MR is frequently detected on intraoperative transesophageal echocardiography or predischarge transthoracic echocardiography, and whether mild residual MR is acceptable remains clinically controversial. Existing evidence derives largely from single-center studies with limited sample sizes, and the timing of residual MR assessment, grading thresholds, and outcome definitions vary considerably across studies, limiting the generalizability of their conclusions. We therefore plan to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis. PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) will be systematically searched for English-language studies of adults undergoing surgical mitral valve repair for MR of any etiology that report residual MR grade and long-term follow-up outcomes. The primary outcomes are recurrent MR (≥ moderate MR during follow-up) and mitral valve reintervention (surgical or transcatheter). In the primary analysis, adjusted hazard ratios will be pooled using random-effects models; unadjusted estimates will be pooled separately as supplementary analyses and will not be combined with adjusted estimates. Pooled estimates will be obtained separately for different residual MR thresholds (≥ mild vs. none/trace; > mild vs. ≤ mild). Subgroup analyses will be performed according to MR etiology (degenerative vs. other or mixed etiologies) and timing of residual MR assessment (intraoperative vs. early postoperative/predischarge vs. not specified), and the association of residual MR with long-term mortality will also be explored. Because death precludes subsequent reintervention, we will record whether included studies accounted for competing risks, and cause-specific and subdistribution hazard ratios will be pooled together in the primary analysis, with the measure type examined as a subgroup factor and a sensitivity analysis restricted to cause-specific hazard ratios. These analyses will be complemented by risk-of-bias assessment, sensitivity analyses (including recurrent MR defined as ≥ moderate-to-severe MR and reintervention restricted to surgical reoperation), and grading of the certainty of evidence. This study is expected to clarify the prognostic value of residual MR, particularly mild residual MR, thereby providing evidence to inform whether surgeons should aim for no or trace residual MR intraoperatively, whether a second pump run for re-repair is warranted, and how high-risk patients should be stratified for postoperative surveillance, as well as offering a reference for standardizing the definition and reporting of residual MR in future studies.

title: Von Willebrand Factor Biomarkers in Prosthetic Valve Dysfunction
authors: Sameed Arshad; Sabir Khan; Muhammad Zahid
abstract: Imaging remains the foundation of prosthetic valve surveillance because it identifies valve morphology, lesion mechanism, and hemodynamic severity. However, acoustic shadowing, eccentric or multiple regurgitant jets, loading conditions, and reader variability can complicate assessment, particularly for paravalvular regurgitation after transcatheter aortic valve replacement. High shear stress unfolds von Willebrand factor (VWF), promotes proteolysis of its high-molecular-weight multimers, and produces a measurable defect in primary hemostasis. Multimer analysis, closure time with adenosine diphosphate (CT-ADP), and the VWF activity-to-antigen ratio therefore provide a biologic signal of abnormal flow rather than an anatomic image. Prospective studies show that VWF abnormalities track residual paravalvular regurgitation during transcatheter aortic valve replacement, occur with dysfunctional prostheses, change after mitral paravalvular-leak repair, and are associated with bleeding. The evidence nevertheless remains observational; most diagnostic cohorts are small and single-center, thresholds lack independent validation, assays are vulnerable to hematologic and preanalytic confounding, and no completed randomized trial has shown that VWF-guided management improves outcomes. VWF testing is best viewed as an investigational adjunct when imaging and the clinical picture are discordant or when prosthetic dysfunction coexists with otherwise unexplained bleeding. It should not replace guideline-directed echocardiography or be used for routine surveillance outside research protocols.

title: Association between preoperative E/e′ and early left ventricular systolic recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting
authors: Jungsuk Choi; Hee Kyung Kim; Joon Kyu Kang
abstract: Background In patients with reduced or mildly reduced ejection fraction, the degree of systolic recovery after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) is heterogeneous. We assessed whether routine preoperative transthoracic echocardiography (TTE) indices—particularly E/e′—are associated with early postoperative improvement in left ventricular function. Methods We retrospectively analyzed patients undergoing isolated CABG at a single tertiary center (April 2019 to July 2025). Eligibility required a preoperative left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) of <50%. Emergency/salvage operations, 30-day deaths, and patients without an evaluable early postoperative TTE were excluded. The primary outcome was an absolute increase in the LVEF of ≥10 percentage points. Because of the limited number of outcome events, the primary association analysis used a single-predictor logistic regression model with preoperative E/e′. Sensitivity analyses excluded patients with preoperative atrial fibrillation (AF) and modeled postoperative LVEF as a continuous outcome adjusted for baseline LVEF. Results Of 75 otherwise clinically eligible patients, three lacked an evaluable early postoperative TTE, leaving 72 patients for outcome analysis; 17 (23.6%) achieved an LVEF increase of ≥10 percentage points. A higher preoperative E/e′ was associated with early LVEF improvement (OR 1.155 per 1-unit increase; 95% CI 1.04–1.28; p = 0.005; N = 66; 16 events). The apparent AUC was 0.700; after 1,000-resample bootstrap internal validation, the estimated optimism was 0.004 and the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.696 (95% bootstrap CI 0.526–0.885). The association persisted after excluding patients with AF (OR 1.14; 95% CI 1.02–1.27; p = 0.025). In a sensitivity analysis using postoperative LVEF as a continuous outcome, E/e′ remained associated with postoperative LVEF after adjustment for baseline LVEF ( β = 0.31 percentage points per 1-unit increase; 95% CI 0.01–0.61; p = 0.042). Conclusion A higher preoperative E/e′ was associated with early improvement in LV systolic function after CABG among patients with a preoperative LVEF of <50% who survived to undergo early postoperative echocardiographic assessment. Given the small number of events and the single-center retrospective design, these findings are hypothesis-generating and require external validation.

title: Clinical manifestations of resistance to thyroid hormone beta (RTHβ) syndrome in children – multicenter case series
authors: Anna Fedorczak; Martyna Sokół; Iwona Beń‐Skowronek; Magdalena Mierzwa; Agnieszka Zachurzok; Agnieszka Bogusz-Wójcik; Julia Przybylak-Ortega; Elżbieta Moszczyńska; Paulina Berezowiec; Artur Bossowski; Natalia Dąbek; Artur Mazur; Kamil Dyrka; Marek Niedziela; Magdalena Makowiecka-Wolek; Robert Stanisław Śmigiel; Agnieszka Ulenberg; Małgorzata Myśliwiec; Renata Stawerska
abstract: Introduction Resistance to thyroid hormone (TH) β (RTHβ) is a rare genetic disorder caused by mutations in the TH receptor β gene ( THRB ) and characterized by elevated TH levels with non-suppressed thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) and variable clinical presentation. The aim of the study was to characterize the clinical and biochemical features of children with RTHβ, correlate them with genetic findings and therapeutic management, to raise clinicians’ awareness of the specific characteristics of the condition. Material and methods This retrospective multicenter case series included 15 children with genetically confirmed THRB variants. Clinical, laboratory, imaging, and treatment data were analyzed retrospectively. Results All the patients demonstrated elevated free thyroxine and free triiodothyronine concentrations with detectable, non-suppressed TSH serum level. Common findings included tachycardia (73%), neurodevelopmental disturbances (60%), and a lean phenotype (BMI <10th percentile, 53%). Misdiagnosis of primary hyperthyroidism occurred in 20% of cases. Most patients did not require pharmacological treatment or were managed with beta-blockers alone for symptomatic tachycardia control. Discussion Pediatric RTHβ shows consistent biochemical features but marked clinical heterogeneity. Awareness is essential to ensure accurate diagnosis and avoid unnecessary therapy.

title: Beyond the clinic: a six-month home-based exercise and respiratory rehabilitation program improves functional capacity, respiratory muscle strength, and fatigue in chronic heart failure
authors: Mariusz Ciołkiewicz; Mariusz Wojciuk; Anna Kuryliszyn-Moskal; Agnieszka Dakowicz; Emilia Sawicka; Karol Adam Kamiński
abstract: Introduction Optimal models of rehabilitation dedicated for patients with heart failure (HF) remain under investigation. The aim of this study was to assess the safety and effectiveness of a 6-month home-based rehabilitation program in patients with HF. Materials and methods 63 patients with stable HF were randomized, 28 patients from intervention group completed the study and were included in the analysis. Assessments including the 6-minute walk test, respiratory muscle strength, and quality of life measures (SF-36 and Fatigue Severity Scale – FSS) were conducted at baseline and after 6 months. Additionally, adverse events and adherence to the training protocol were monitored. Results Due to objective challenges caused by the COVID-19 pandemic outbreak, the course and final outcomes of the study differed from the original protocol; the control group was not assessed after 6 months. In the intervention group, 6 months of rehabilitation resulted in statistically significant improvements: the 6-minute walk distance increased by 37.86 meters ( p = 0.001), maximal inspiratory pressure (PImax) improved by 20.21 cmH₂O, and maximal expiratory pressure (PEmax) by 20.75 cmH₂O (both p < 0.01). A significant reduction in fatigue was observed, as measured by FSS, with a mean decrease of 0.68 points ( p = 0.029). Adherence to the exercise protocol averaged 91.5 ± 15.3%. No serious adverse events were reported. Conclusions The home-based rehabilitation program, including respiratory muscle training, is safe and effective for patients with chronic HF. It improves functional capacity and reduces fatigue levels. Clinical Trial registration https://clinicaltrials.gov/ct2/show/NCT03780803 , ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03780803. Registered 19/12/2018.

title: VARIATIONS IN BRANCHING PATTERN OF THE LEFT CORONARY ARTERY AND CLINICAL SIGNIFICANCE OF TRIANGLE OF BROCQ AND MOUCHET: CADAVERIC STUDY
journal: International Journal of Drug Delivery Technology
abstract: Background: The left coronary artery (LCA) shows marked anatomical variability in its branching pattern, which is crucial for interventional and surgical procedures.The Triangle of Brocq and Mouchet (TBM), formed by the left anterior descending artery (LAD), left circumflex artery (LCx), and great cardiac vein (GCV), is a key yet under-explored coronary landmark with clinical and radiological significance.Methods: Thirty human cadaveric hearts from routine dissections were studied to document LCA origin, branching patterns, and TBM morphology.The LCA was classified as bifurcating, trifurcating, quadrifurcating, or pentafurcating.The TBM was evaluated for its presence, completeness, shape, and contents.The positional relationship of the GCV with the LAD and LCx was also assessed.Results: TBM was present in all specimens, predominantly in a closed form (80%), followed by inferiorly (10%) and superiorly (10%) open types.The triangle commonly contained a median artery (36.7%), diagonal branch (26.7%), or both (6.7%); one specimen showed a GCV tributary.LCA branching patterns included bifurcation (50%), trifurcation (20%), quadrifurcation (20%), and pentafurcation (10%).The GCV was superficial to the LAD in 33.3% and deep in 66.7%, while superficial to the LCx in 60% and deep in 40% of cases.Conclusion: This study highlights notable variability in LCA branching and TBM configuration, with the closed triangle being most common.Awareness of these variations is essential during coronary interventions and bypass grafting to prevent iatrogenic injury and improve procedural accuracy.

title: Evaluation of mitral regurgitation severity in type 1 acute myocardial infarction: correlation with wall motion score index and infarct location
authors: Irine Ferza Sulfiker; Shalaka S Ramgir; Shreeyash Tulpule; Sammita Jadhav
abstract: Ischemic mitral regurgitation (MR) is One common and important prognostic consequence of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). Although it is frequently used to evaluate ventricular function, left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) may underestimate early localized dysfunction that contributes to MR. To determine whether WMSI provides additional clinical value for the early assessment of MR severity in patients with acute myocardial infarction undergoing PCI, future prospective, multicenter trials involving longitudinal follow-up are necessary. 218 patients with type 1 AMI who were assessed before PCI at a tertiary care facility between January 2024 and July 2025 were included in this cross-sectional observational analysis. Every individual had transthoracic echocardiography to determine the site of the infarct, WMSI, LVEF, and MR severity using a multiparametric method. Chi-square tests and ordinal logistic regression were used to examine relationships between MR grade and clinical, demographic, and echocardiographic factors. Grade 2 MR (44.4%) was the most prevalent among 218 patients, followed by Grade 1 (26.1%) and Grade 3 (25.2%). While lower LVEF was linked to higher MR severity, higher BMI, older age, larger LA diameter, male sex, and hypertension were all independently linked to rising MR grade. MR grade was not independently correlated with WMSI (OR = 1.985, 95% CI: 0.703–5.681; p = 0.197). Only SWMI among infarct areas was significantly correlated with MR grade (OR = 0.071, 95% CI: 0.008–0.480; p = 0.010). Similar discrimination was shown by ROC analysis for LVEF (AUC = 0.800, 95% CI: 0.742–0.858) and WMSI (AUC = 0.794, 95% CI: 0.726–0.862). The degree of mitral regurgitation in individuals with type 1 acute myocardial infarction prior to PCI indicates both localized and widespread left ventricular dysfunction. Beyond traditional LVEF evaluation, the Wall Motion Score Index may improve early risk classification as a sensitive early indication of ischemia MR. Not applicable.

title: Endoscopic secondary chordae transfer and edge-to-edge repair for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse
authors: Martina Giusti; Can Gollmann-Tepeköylü; Leo Pölzl; Hannes Abfalterer; Daniel Höfer; Nikolaos Bonaros
abstract: Anterior leaflet prolapse remains a challenging lesion in mitral valve repair, particularly in the presence of asymmetric degenerative disease. We present the case of a 59-year-old patient with severe mitral regurgitation due to asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse in the setting of Barlow's disease, treated through a totally endoscopic right minithoracotomy. Intraoperative valve analysis demonstrated prolapse of the A2M2 and A3 segments with elongated secondary chordae. Mitral valve repair was performed using secondary chordae transfer, followed by asymmetric edge-to-edge repair at the A2-P2 scallops and ring annuloplasty. Intraoperative assessment showed satisfactory leaflet coaptation with trivial residual regurgitation. Postoperative echocardiography confirmed the absence of residual mitral regurgitation and no evidence of clinically significant mitral stenosis. This report describes the technical aspects of endoscopic secondary chordae transfer combined with asymmetric edge-to-edge repair and ring annuloplasty for the treatment of asymmetric anterior leaflet prolapse, demonstrating the feasibility of this repair strategy in a complex mitral valve anatomy.

title: Assessment of Atrioventricular and Ventriculoarterial Coupling Indices in Patients with Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome Utilizing Cardiac MRI and Invasive Hemodynamics

title: Quality of online mastitis management information for dairy farmers in India: an evaluation of Hindi language YouTube videos
authors: D. A. K. Reddy; Dadimi Bhargavi; Rupasi Tiwari; A G Adeeth Cariappa
abstract: Abstract YouTube has become a primary informal extension channel for livestock health information in India, yet quality is unregulated and algorithmically driven by popularity rather than accuracy. This study systematically evaluates the quality of Hindi language YouTube videos on Mastitis which is one of the most economically significant dairy diseases in India, using four validated instruments modified DISCERN (mDISCERN), JAMA benchmark criteria, Global Quality Scale (GQS), and a purpose-built Mastitis Video Content Scoring (MVCS) tool. We searched YouTube using the YouTube Data API v3 with four Hindi language queries on 6 March 2026, screened 200 videos, and analysed 63 that met inclusion criteria. Most videos were low quality: mean GQS was 1.98/5, mean JAMA was 1.21/4 and mean mDISCERN was 1.96/5. Independent creators produced 52% of videos and achieved the highest audience reach (Video Power Index: 2.32), yet scored lowest on clinical comprehensiveness. Veterinary professionals produced fewer videos but achieved the highest quality scores and engagement ratios (4.26), suggesting trust driven rather than algorithm driven audiences. A weak positive correlation between video duration and MVCS (r = 0.265, p = 0.036) indicates that longer run time is not a prerequisite for comprehensive content. These findings reveal a critical popularity-quality gap in digital veterinary extension and highlight the need to build digital communication capacity among field-level veterinarians.

title: Case Report: Discordant hypertrophic cardiomyopathy in monozygotic twins with LEOPARD syndrome and an identical PTPN11 c.1391G > C (p.Gly464Ala) mutation
authors: Xin Xue; Yayuan Ning; Fang Yao; Xiaowei Zhang; Xianjing Song
abstract: LEOPARD syndrome (LS; Noonan syndrome with multiple lentigines) is a rare autosomal dominant RASopathy in which PTPN11 mutations cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM) with highly variable expressivity. We report adolescent monozygotic twin brothers carrying an identical PTPN11 c.1391G > C (p.Gly464Ala) mutation that arose de novo , who developed discordant cardiac phenotypes despite sharing a genome and an intrauterine and postnatal environment. The younger twin developed obstructive HCM with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve and left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (peak resting gradient 36 mmHg, peak Valsalva gradient 61 mmHg), together with pectus excavatum and macroglossia; the older twin had non-obstructive HCM (maximal septal thickness 12 mm) with a patent foramen ovale. Both twins had multiple lentigines, facial dysmorphism, and sensorineural hearing loss requiring cochlear implantation. The younger twin was treated with a beta-blocker and activity restriction, whereas the older twin was managed with surveillance alone. This case demonstrates that an identical RASopathy mutation can produce divergent forms of HCM, supports a role for non-genetic modifiers in cardiovascular expression, and underscores the need for hemodynamics-guided, individualized cardiovascular management in LS.

title: Influence of the Angiotensin Receptor Neprilysin Inhibitor Compared with Perindopril on Left Atrial Strain and Prognosis in Heart Failure

title: The correlation between epicardial adipose tissue thickness and left ventricular systolic function in patients with systemic lupus erythematosus
authors: Sisi Lin; Shengmin Zhang; Hui Zhou
abstract: Background Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) can cause myocardial damage and left ventricular dysfunction in patients. Abnormal deposition of epicardial adipose tissue (EAT) can promote the occurrence and development of cardiovascular diseases. The aim of this study was to investigate changes in EAT thickness in patients with SLE and apply two-dimensional speckle tracking echocardiography (2D-STE) to study the correlation between EAT and left ventricular systolic function. Patients and methods This case–control study recruited a total of 67 SLE patients as the case group and 31 healthy individuals as the control group. Left ventricular systolic function parameters were measured using 2D-STE. Changes and correlations in laboratory indicators, EAT, and left ventricular systolic function parameters were compared between groups. Results Compared with the control group, the case group showed significantly increased EAT and diastolic left ventricular posterior wall thickness (LVPWD) ( P <0.05). High-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C), apical two-chamber longitudinal strain (AP2C LS), apical three-chamber longitudinal strain (AP3C LS), apical four-chamber longitudinal strain (AP4C LS), and global longitudinal strain (GLS) were significantly reduced ( P < 0.05). The 18-segment left ventricular longitudinal strain was further grouped according to coronary artery supply; the LAD, RCA, and LCX groups in the patient cohort all showed reductions compared with the healthy control group ( P < 0.05). Spearman correlation analysis revealed that EAT was negatively correlated with GLS ( r = −0.39, P < 0.05), LAD group ( r = −0.26, P < 0.05), RCA group ( r = −0.47, P < 0.05), and LCX group ( r = −0.29, P < 0.05), and positively correlated with duration of illness (DT) ( r = 0.41, P < 0.05) and age ( r = 0.45, P < 0.05). Multiple linear regression analysis confirmed that EAT is an important influencing factor of left ventricular longitudinal strain function ( P < 0.05). Conclusion Increased epicardial adipose tissue thickness is negatively correlated with left ventricular systolic function. EAT can effectively reflect changes in left ventricular systolic function in SLE patients, providing a basis for clinical management and early intervention.
